The transcription factor XBP1s, a key effector of the UPR’s IRE1α branch, has been implicated in plasma cell differentiation, but its role in early B cell development and tolerance remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that sustained activation of XBP1s shapes anergic B cell development and peripheral tolerance. We generated a B cell-specific XBP1s knock-in mouse model that induces chronic XBP1s expression. We find that chronic XBP1s overexpression drives the accumulation of anergic transitional 3 B cells, which exhibits attenuated activation responses to both BCR and TLR stimulation. Mechanistically, XBP1s overexpression upregulates the anergy-associated factor Egr2 and suppresses Irf4 expression. Our study provides insights into how dysregulated XBP1s expression may contribute to immune tolerance and dysfunction.

title: Molecular mechanisms of NLR proteins in inflammasome activation
abstract: Nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeat-containing proteins (NLRs) are central mediators of inflammasome signaling, activating caspase-1 to drive pyroptotic cell death and pro-inflammatory responses. Although NLR activation is generally thought to involve conformational rearrangements that oligomerize their N- or C-terminal death domains to nucleate ASC or pro-caspase-1 oligomerization, the molecular mechanisms that enable these transitions vary substantially among family members. Here, we highlight recent structural advances that reveal how distinct NLRs are activated and assemble into higher-order signaling platforms, providing mechanistic insights into the diverse activation mechanisms that converge on a common inflammatory outcome.

title: PATZ1 remodels the nucleosome landscape to promote chromatin accessibility in injured neurons
abstract: Adult central nervous system neurons fail to regenerate after injury, in part due to epigenetic constraints that maintain a growth-restrictive chromatin state. We previously showed that the transcription factor PATZ1 reprograms chromatin accessibility in injured corticospinal neurons and primes the regeneration associated gene loci, but the underlying mechanism remained unclear. Here we use nucleosome-resolution profiling to reveal that PATZ1 induces widespread nucleosome eviction at regeneration-associated gene loci. PATZ1 overexpression (PATZ1 OE) dramatically reduces both nucleosome occupancy and fuzziness, indicating active chromatin reorganization rather than passive destabilization. This reorganization occurs preferentially at distal regulatory elements, where PATZ1 drives a greater than 3-fold expansion of H3K27ac-marked active enhancers. Nucleosome eviction at these sites likely helps in enhancer activation, establishing a mechanistic link between chromatin reorganization and transcriptional reprogramming. Our findings demonstrate that targeted nucleosome eviction at enhancers underlies PATZ1-mediated chromatin reorganization, providing mechanistic insight into the epigenetic barriers that constrain regenerative gene expression in the central nervous system (CNS).

title: Author Correction: B7-H3 promotes skin photodamage through ITGA2-NRF2-TFAM-mediated mitochondrial oxidative stress
abstract: In the version of the article initially published, the “WT, COL3A1” image in Fig. 3i was a duplicate of the “KO, COL1A1” image due to an error in figure assembly. Fig. 3i has now been updated to include the correct “WT, COL3A1” image in the HTML and PDF versions of the article

title: Evolution towards higher unitary conductance in mammals makes BK channels more efficient and precise
abstract: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. Mammalian BK channels are distinguished by an exceptionally high unitary conductance (~250 pS), while invertebrates exhibit a significantly lower unitary conductance. We confirmed the evolutionary trend to high unitary conductance and used computational models to examine how differences in unitary conductance affect calcium activation of BK channels and influence neuronal dynamics. We show that mammalian BK channels are activated more efficiently by calcium and generate stronger repolarizing currents than lower unitary conductance channels. Channels with lower unitary conductance require greater channel density in the cell membrane, leading to stronger competition for calcium and reduced activation. In contrast, high unitary conductance channels minimize competition, enabling more effective activation and repolarization. Incorporating these channel properties into a neuronal model revealed that mammalian-type BK channels enhance spike-timing precision, consistent with the evolution of fine motor control and advanced neuronal processing in mammals.
keywords: Ion channels in the nervous system

title: Pooled CRISPR screens identify genes and non-coding genomic regions that regulate red blood cell density
abstract: Genome-wide association studies have identified >1000 loci associated with red blood cell (RBC) traits. However, few of these associations have been functionally characterized. Here, we performed pooled CRISPR screens in an erythroid cell line to identify genes and regulatory non-coding sequences that control RBC density. We perturbed 556 candidate genes and genomic sequences near 2114 GWAS variants. After validation, we found 17 genes and 13 regions near GWAS variants, implicating known (e.g. ATP2B4 , CCND3 , EPOR ) and novel (e.g. CHTF8 , CTU2 , DNASE2 , RAB10 ) genes. We confirmed that deletions in the osmotic stress response kinase gene OXSR1 increase cell density. We also combined CRISPR perturbations and RNA-sequencing to show how a non-coding genomic sequence near rs13255015 regulates the expression of the transcription factor ZFAT in cis and SLC4A1 in trans . Our results suggest experimental strategies to characterize GWAS findings and provide new molecular insights into the regulation of complex RBC traits.

title: Distinct roles of the Lyve1 lineage in mouse heart development
abstract: The genetic mouse model Lyve1 Cre is widely used to study lymphatic endothelial cells, but its activity in the embryonic heart has not been comprehensively defined. Here we show that the Lyve1 lineage contributes to multiple cardiovascular cell types, including venous endothelium of the sinus venosus forming coronary vessels, endocardial cells generating complementary coronary territories and valve structures, lymphatic endothelial cells required for cardiac lymphatic development, and tissue-resident macrophages within the embryonic myocardium. Functional perturbations studies show that Notch1 gain-of-function in Lyve1 + lineages disrupts vascular development, whereas Prox1 deletion causes severe edema, blood-filled lymphatics, and perinatal lethality. Mid-gestation mutants exhibit underdeveloped blood-filled lymphatics despite intact blood vasculature, and by late gestation cardiac lymphatics are largely depleted. These findings reveal distinct cardiovascular roles of the Lyve1 lineage and establish Lyve1 Cre as a versatile but non-specific model, underscoring the need for careful interpretation when investigating heart development and regeneration.

title: Threshold-free neural network models for swim bout detection of larval zebrafish
abstract: Accurate detection of swim bouts is essential for decoding motor behavior in larval zebrafish, yet conventional threshold-based methods rely on subjective cutoffs and per-experiment tuning. To address this limitation, we developed threshold-free deep learning models operating on tail-curvature time series: an offline model for post hoc analysis and an online model for real-time detection. Both improved precision over threshold-based methods, particularly for low-amplitude bouts. Using the offline model, we show that a head-fixed, closed-loop preparation largely preserves naturalistic swimming kinematics. Repeated trials reduced bout frequency and increased interbout interval, whereas genetic background primarily affects bout duration and maximum amplitude; notably, casper larvae lacked the late-trial decline observed in wildtype and nacre. We further show that detector choice can alter inferred behavioral outcomes. Together, these results establish a high-throughput framework for robust and reproducible analysis of zebrafish swimming behavior across experimental conditions.

title: Extragonadal role of FSH in regulating corneal homeostasis in Keratoconus
abstract: Keratoconus (KC) is a multifactorial, progressive, ectatic disease of the cornea, which often manifests during puberty. The clinical phenotype includes progressive loss of stromal collagen, with emerging evidence indicating inflammation contributes to the disease pathology. In this study, we investigated the extragonadal role of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in corneal stromal collagen degradation and inflammation. Using a 3D collagen hydrogel system, co-culture models, and patient-derived tears, we found the following: FSH levels were low in KC patients; FSH supplementation inhibited MAP kinase signaling, leading to decreased MMP2 activity and increased collagen accumulation; FSH increased pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion, driving macrophage polarization, migration, and tunneling nanotube formation; FSH regulated the HDAC1-miR-29b feedback loop in chromatin immunoprecipitation and overexpression studies; Gene ontology linked FSH to leukocyte adhesion and extravasation; and Motif analysis identified NF-Y as a possible HDAC1-interacting partner. Collectively, FSH plays a dual role in keratoconus by regulating collagen accumulation through the MAP Kinase-MMP2 axis and inflammation through the HDAC1-miR-29b pathway.

title: Individualized morphometric-similarity deviations in autism linked to cortical hierarchy and microarchitecture
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows marked interindividual variation that complicates efforts to identify coherent neuroanatomical signatures. Here we combine subject-wise morphometric-similarity networks with hierarchical Bayesian normative regression to map per-region, per-subject departures from expected cortical organization across 308 parcels in a large multisite cohort. Normative z-maps reveal that ASD individuals have a higher prevalence of extreme, spatially focal deviations than controls, yet fewer than 12% of cases show extreme deviation in any single region. These deviations are not random: they preferentially redistribute morphometric similarity from association and heteromodal cortex toward sensory and visual territories and align with canonical cortical gradients. Network-level analyses identify a spatially localized subnetwork of altered similarity (dominant in occipito-temporal/visual nodes). Semi-supervised clustering of individual z-maps resolves a reproducible continuous axis of deviation whose opposite ends carry opposite global polarity and distinct cortical-molecular couplings revealed by transcriptomic and neurotransmitter-receptor density maps, as well as divergent cognitive meta-analytic associations. Together, these findings reframe ASD neuroanatomy as gradient-constrained and molecularly tethered at the individual level and support normative, subject-wise approaches for mechanism-informed stratification.

title: Maltreatment predicts centiles of individual variation from normative brain growth in children
abstract: Exposure to maltreatment in childhood is posited to profoundly disrupt brain development with adverse consequences for cognitive development and health across the lifespan. Here we use “brain charts” from the largest available neuroimaging database to quantify individual brain volumes relative to normative brain growth distributions in 299 children, aged 3 to 13 years, including 123 children with clinically verified maltreatment exposure. Using magnetic resonance imaging, we obtain volumes of cortical grey, total white, and subcortical grey matter and derive chart-based centiles for each child and tissue type. In our sample, children with maltreatment exposure exhibit lower mean brain centiles across tissues than unexposed children. Associations of greater maltreatment severity with lower brain centiles do not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Lower brain centiles are associated with lower intellectual ability and more behavioural problems. These findings provide evidence for widespread differences in brain structure associated with childhood maltreatment and their relevance to intellectual ability and behavioural functioning.

title: Emerging links between gut dysbiosis, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation, and Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD), the second most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder, is classically defined as a motor disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra and motor dysfunction. Increasing evidence, however, identifies PD as a multisystem disorder with early non-motor features, including sleep, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal disturbances, implicating the gut-brain axis. Tryptophan metabolism through serotonin, kynurenine, and indole pathways generates bioactive metabolites, many of which regulate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic metabolism through canonical signaling pathways; however, growing evidence supports its role in immune balance, glial responses, and barrier integrity. Altered AhR signaling may therefore connect gut dysbiosis and disrupted tryptophan metabolism to sustained, systemic and central inflammation in PD. This review examines gut dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism, and AhR signaling as potential mechanisms underlying idiopathic PD and highlights their relevance to early diagnosis and disease-modifying therapies.

title: Predicting transcriptional burst kinetics from histone modifications with deep learning
abstract: Transcription is inherently bursty, and burst frequency and burst size provide mechanistically informative phenotypes that are not uniquely determined by mean expression alone. Yet it remains difficult to quantify, at genome scale, how histone-modification landscapes encode these burst kinetics. Here we show that DeepBurst, a deep learning model, predicts gene-specific burst-frequency and burst-size regimes from histone-modification profiles around transcription start sites. DeepBurst uses self-attention to learn combinatorial, position-dependent predictive patterns, with training labels inferred from single-cell transcriptome data using mechanistic bursting models. Across three human cell lines and two label-inference procedures, DeepBurst achieves consistent performance under chromosome-based splits and shows strong cross-cell type generalization. Model interpretation shows that burst frequency benefits from broader chromatin context, whereas burst size depends more strongly on promoter-proximal signals. Model-constrained in silico perturbations further identify histone-profile changes predicted to shift bursting regimes. DeepBurst therefore enables genome-wide mapping from readily measurable histone-modification landscapes to hard-to-assay transcriptional bursting dynamics, while generating testable hypotheses for future perturbation studies.

title: Hepatitis E virus genome plasticity: a marker of chronicity and therapy failure?
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a globally distributed zoonotic pathogen, spread by contaminated food and blood products, and a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis. Recent data indicate that the HEV genome contains a highly heterogeneous hypervariable region (HVR) that can tolerate extensive genomic rearrangements, especially among immunocompromised patients. These rearrangements can increase HEV replication in tissue-culture and have further been observed in HEV-infected patients. Insertions comprise either duplications of virus-derived sequences, or alternatively, host-derived sequence fragments and exhibit enrichment of specific amino acids and functional motifs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving these insertions, as well as their functional significance, remain largely unexplored. Given that sequences not required for infectivity or replication are typically rapidly eliminated in small RNA viruses such as HEV, the persistence of HVR insertions suggests a potential biological role in HEV replication and/or pathogenesis. This review summarizes our current understanding of the role of HVR insertions during HEV infection, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying these insertions. We further discuss the factors driving the selection of genomic insertions and speculate on their functional role by analyzing over 650 publicly available HEV genotype 3 genome sequences and systematically cataloging identified insertions.

title: Identification of candidate key genes involved in natural rubber biosynthesis in Periploca sepium
abstract: Natural rubber is a critical industrial material facing supply shortages. Periploca sepium has emerged as a promising alternative for producing the rubber component cis -polyisoprene. To investigate its biosynthesis, we performed genome and transcriptome sequencing. Our results indicate that this plant possesses complete mevalonic acid (MVA), 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate/2-C-methyl-D-erythritol-4-phosphate (DXP/MEP), and polyisoprene pathways, as well as contains corresponding rubber particle membrane proteins. Using weighted gene co-expression network analysis, we identified 11 key genes positively correlated with levels of cis -polyisoprene and precursor allylic diphosphates (IPP/DMAPP, GPP, FPP, GGPP). Overexpressing acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, and 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate reductoisomerase genes from the MVA and DXP/MEP pathways in P. sepium increased IPP/DMAPP levels. Molecular docking and enzyme assays indicated that cis -prenyltransferase exhibits the highest affinity for FPP, suggesting it is the dominant initiator of IPP condensation in cis -polyisoprene biosynthesis. Overexpressing the FPP synthase gene enhanced FPP levels, leading to increased cis -poly7isoprene content. Overexpressing cis -prenyltransferase, small rubber particle protein, and rubber elongation factor genes, especially in combination, significantly raised cis -polyisoprene content and high-molecular-weight proportions. These findings demonstrate that targeted gene up-regulation can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium .

title: In vivo replication of a fully functional nerve net in a clonally reproducing animal
abstract: Nerve nets are considered the evolutionarily oldest form of nervous system. How such networks develop and how complex nervous systems become fully functional is largely unknown. In a phylogenetically ancient animal, the freshwater polyp Hydra , we demonstrate how a nerve net consisting of distinct neuronal populations is precisely replicated over the course of asexual proliferation by budding. During this process, precursor cells first accumulate at the site of the emerging neural network, followed by a stepwise formation of functional neural circuits composed of distinct neuronal populations. These circuits become arranged according to an accurately controlled spatiotemporal pattern and take control of behaviors independently of the existing parental network. Since similar processes also govern the formation of more complex nervous systems in other invertebrates and vertebrates, we suggest that the basic requirements for a neuronal network to replicate were already in place at the beginning of the evolution of the nervous system.

title: Dysregulation of the Hippo pathway enhances PD-L2 transcription to promote immune evasion in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: The Hippo pathway and its downstream effectors, YAP/TAZ, exhibit aberrant regulation in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, facilitating cancer cell growth. However, the influence of YAP/TAZ on cancer immune evasion remains poorly understood. Herein, we show that cancer patients harboring mutations regulating the Hippo pathway and YAP/TAZ hyperactivation may be sensitized to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy owing to genome instability and PD-L2 expression. LATS1/2 deletion, accompanied by YAP/TAZ hyperactivation, was associated with loss of squamous differentiation and genome instability, which may contribute to elevated DNA damage. Our data suggest that YAP/TAZ may recruit TEAD, BRD4, and RNA polymerase Ⅱ to the super-enhancer and promoter regions of PD-L1 and PD-L2 . YAP/TAZ predominantly contribute to PD-L2 expression, which is associated with Stat3 activation, partially enhancing PD-L1 transcription. YAP/TAZ-activated cells can be targeted by antigen-specific T cells but evade them through PD-L2. These findings suggest that Hippo pathway alterations and associated YAP/TAZ hyperactivation may serve as potential prognostic factors for stratifying patients undergoing ICI therapy. Targeting YAP/TAZ/TEAD could offer a promising treatment avenue for cancers harboring YAP/TAZ hyperactivation.

title: Hdac3 shapes adipocyte size, death susceptibility, macrophage turnover, and vascular remodeling in a mouse model of obesity
abstract: The crosstalk between adipocytes and macrophages is crucial in adipose tissue biology. The aim of this study was to investigate the role of adipocyte-expressed histone deacetylase 3 (Hdac3) on adipose tissue plasticity and immune cell composition in response to high-fat feeding. Here we show that adipocyte-specific deletion of Hdac3 gene in mice affects the response to high-fat overload, by reducing fat mass and adipocyte size in visceral fat of knockout mice. In the absence of adipocyte Hdac3, visceral fat shows vascular remodeling and increased macrophage content. Colocalization of F4/80 with Ki-67 indicates proliferation of resident macrophages. This is coupled with increased crown-like structures and adipocyte death in visceral fat of knockout mice, exacerbated by high-fat feeding. Hdac3 silencing in cultured adipocytes and inactivation in mice promotes a pro-apoptotic microenvironment, as assessed by positivity to Annexin V and cleaved Caspase 3. In conclusion, we propose that Hdac3 acts as a rheostat in visceral fat, differentially affecting lipid accumulation and adipocyte size during the progress of high fat diet (HFD) feeding, and limiting cell death, vascularization, and macrophage proliferation, in a mouse model of obesity.

title: Relationship between X chromosome mosaicism, neuroanatomy and cognitive performance in females
abstract: Females have two X chromosomes, one of which is inactivated early in development with specific regions and genes ‘escaping’ inactivation. Thus, X chromosome loss putatively results in decreased ‘dosage’ of X chromosome escapee and pseudoautosomal genes, impacting downstream pathways. Evidence from Turner syndrome (TS) indicates that X chromosome monosomy results in consistent neuroanatomical and cognitive phenotypes. However, it remains unclear whether mosaic karyotypes, with mixed proportions of 45X and 46XX cells, attenuate these phenotypes. Using support vector regression, we examined whether X chromosome mosaicism is predicted by features derived from structural brain MRI and neurocognitive assessments of 48 pre- and early pubertal girls with monosomic TS, with mosaic TS, and without TS. Higher proportion of 46XX cells was significantly predicted by structural properties in somatosensory, motor, visual, and language brain areas, and by performance in visuospatial, fine-motor, and language tasks. Thus, mosaicism partially ‘rescues’ phenotypes linked to full 45X monosomy and may explain the role of the X chromosome not only across heterogeneous phenotypic expression in females, but also in sex differences observed in neuropsychiatric conditions.

title: FLASHS reveals multiscale spatial gene programs at atlas scale
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue architecture, but detecting spatially variable genes at atlas scale remains difficult because biologically relevant patterns are multiscale, sparse, and often non-parametric. Here we show that FLASHS, a frequency-domain kernel test using random Fourier features, sparse sketching, and a kurtosis-corrected null, retains Gaussian-kernel flexibility at near-linear per-gene cost without permutation. Across 50 benchmark datasets spanning 9 spatial transcriptomics platforms, FLASHS achieves the highest ranking accuracy among 14 compared methods while maintaining calibrated inference under simulation and full-atlas permutation. In human heart tissue, it recovers a mitochondrial biogenesis program that co-localizes with ventricular cardiomyocytes. On the Allen Brain MERFISH atlas containing 3.94 million cells, FLASHS completes in minutes on a single workstation and separates biological signal from negative-control barcodes even when p -values saturate.

title: A review of self-supervised imaging phenotypes for genome-wide association studies
abstract: Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

title: Single-cell and spatial mapping reveals GCLC+ mesenchymal tumor cells linked with favorable outcomes in TNBC
abstract: Oxidative stress response (OSR) is suggested as a therapeutic target in triple negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, the cell type specificity and spatial distribution of OSR genes and proteins remain poorly defined. We re-analyzed public datasets, demostrating high OSR gene expression in TNBC tumor cells. We generated a multiplex immunofluorescence dataset of 345 TNBC samples that showed OSR proteins GCLC and NQO1 are differentially expressed across tumor, immune, and stromal cells, and elevated in inflamed regions. We identified a mesenchymal-like tumor cell state characterized by co-expression of GCLC and vimentin (GCLC⁺VIM⁺), with increased proliferation and reduced anastasis-associated signatures, suggesting a vulnerability to chemotherapy. Consistently, TNBC cell lines with higher GCLC expression showed increased sensitivity to cisplatin. Moreover, patients with higher proportions of GCLC⁺VIM⁺ tumor cells had longer overall survival. Our findings indicate that OSR proteins are expressed in spatially and phenotypically distinct tumor microenvironments, and that the GCLC⁺VIM⁺ tumor cell state is associated with favorable outcomes in TNBC.

title: Anatid herpesvirus 1 US10 recruits TRIM13 to ubiquitinate STING for autophagic degradation and immune suppression
abstract: The innate immune response is central to antiviral defense, and viruses have evolved sophisticated evasion strategies. Anatid Herpesvirus 1 (AnHV-1) is a pathogenic alphaherpesvirus causing immunosuppression with economic and biosecurity impacts, yet its evasion of immune signaling pathways remains poorly understood. Here we show that AnHV-1 tegument protein US10 suppresses innate immunity by targeting stimulator of interferon genes (STING) for autophagosome-lysosome degradation. US10 associates with STING and binds the autophagy-related protein microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B), enhancing delivery to lysosomes. Mechanistically, US10 recruits E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing protein 13 (TRIM13) and induces stress in the endoplasmic reticulum through the Protein kinase R-like Reticulum Kinase (PERK). These synergistic actions inhibit type I interferon (IFN-I) production and IFN-stimulated gene expression. Deletion of US10 reduces viral replication and pathogenicity while enhancing immune activation in cells and animals. Our findings uncover a dual autophagy-based mechanism of immune evasion and highlight potential therapeutic targets against AnHV-1 and related alphaherpesviruses.

title: Inhibition of spinal astrocytic GPR177 attenuates neuropathic pain by modulating C3/C3aR signaling in male rats
abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) remains refractory to conventional therapy partly because its pathogenesis is incompletely understood. G protein-coupled receptor 177 (GPR177), a multi-pass transmembrane protein, regulates Wnt trafficking and secretion. Here, we use a chronic constriction injury model in male rats and find GPR177 predominantly expresses in spinal astrocytes and co-localizes with complement component 3 (C3). During NP development, astrocytic GPR177 expression increases, accompanied by activation of C3/C3a receptor (C3aR) signaling in the spinal dorsal horn. Gpr177 silencing with siRNA alleviates nerve injury-associated hypersensitivity and reduces the increases in GPR177, glial fibrillary acidic protein, C3, and C3aR. Intrathecal administration of the C3 inhibitor compstatin and the C3aR antagonist SB290157 reduces hypersensitivity and suppresses C3/C3aR activation, supporting the involvement of C3/C3aR signaling in NP development. These findings demonstrate that spinal GPR177 contributes to NP by activating astrocytes and regulating the C3/C3aR signaling pathway, suggesting the GPR177/C3/C3aR axis as a potential therapeutic target for NP.

title: Anatomical differences in the brain organization between Australopithecus and early Homo based on computational neuroanatomy
abstract: Encephalization is a hallmark of human evolution, but how regional brain morphology changed during early hominin evolution remains unclear. Here, we show regional brain morphological differences between sampled Australopithecus and early Homo specimens. Using computed tomography and endocranial casts, we generated brain models for Australopithecus africanus , Homo habilis , and Homo ergaster using an anatomically homogeneous cross-species interpolation technique. Our reconstructions suggest that the posterior cerebellum was enlarged in early Homo compared with the sampled A. africanus specimens. In contrast, relative frontal lobe volume remains largely unchanged among the sampled fossils. We also identify enlargement of temporoparietal regions that, in modern humans, are associated with functions including social communication and tool use. By integrating fossil endocranial morphology with comparative neuroanatomical information from extant primates, the present approach provides a quantitative framework for generating and testing hypotheses about regional brain evolution in extinct hominins.

title: Serum albumin maintains Wnt3a water solubility and activity
abstract: Wnt proteins regulate adult tissue homeostasis and repair by driving stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. High-performance Wnt preparations have enormous therapeutic potential, especially alongside various stem cell technologies. Currently, a major limitation of most Wnt preparations is that they inevitably require fetal bovine serum (FBS) or detergents to maintain Wnt solubility and activity. Recently, afamin (AFM) was identified as a serum factor that solubilizes Wnt3a in conditioned media (CM), obviating the requirement for animal sera. Here, we show that serum albumin (SA) helps maintain the activity and stability of AFM-solubilized Wnt3a in CM, likely through a stabilizing effect. We further demonstrate, using test-tube assays, that SA alone efficiently solubilizes purified Wnt3a (pWnt3a) independently of AFM. This approach enables the conversion of conventional detergent-solubilized pWnt3a (CHAPS–pWnt3a) into SA–pWnt3a through dialysis-mediated detergent removal. Together, these findings define a simple and robust SA-based strategy for preserving Wnt3a activity, addressing a long-standing challenge in both experimental and therapeutic settings.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic insights into conserved and divergent oligodendrocyte lineage programs across species
abstract: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLLCs) are essential for myelination and neuronal homeostasis, yet the evolutionary conservation of their transcriptional programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated approximately one million hippocampal single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from humans, rhesus macaques, cynomolgus macaques, and mice. OLLCs emerged as among the most evolutionarily conserved neural cell populations, with oligodendrocyte precursor cells exhibiting highly conserved transcriptional identities, whereas mature oligodendrocytes displayed greater species-specific diversification We identified evolutionarily divergent genes, including the primate-specific gene CNDP1, and uncovered a species-specific temporal shift of the transcription factor ETV1 during oligodendrocyte differentiation. Cross-species analysis of aging revealed conserved chromatin-regulatory programs together with species-specific aging signatures, including coordinated remodeling of a primate-specific Wnt regulatory network in primate OPCs, whereas aged mouse OPCs were enriched for ribosome biogenesis. Disease-risk signatures further underscore the involvement of OLLCs in neurological disorders. Together, these findings provide a comparative framework for understanding mammalian myelin biology, brain aging, and disease.

title: A role for the BBSome in restricting the entry of non-ciliary proteins into cilia
abstract: Cilia possess the inherent ability to restrict the entry of non-ciliary components through the ciliary gate. Mutations in genes encoding components of the ciliary gate result in various cilia-related diseases known as ciliopathies. Yet, how non-ciliary residents are prevented from accumulating in cilia remains unclear. Here, we observe ciliary accumulation of non-ciliary proteins in BBSome-deficient mutants (Bardet-Biedl syndrome), a phenotype reminiscent of ciliary gate-defective mutants such as mks-5 and nphp-4 . Time-lapse imaging shows that these non-ciliary proteins move bidirectionally along cilia at IFT velocities, and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) reveals that the non-ciliary protein ELMD-1 associates with the IFT component IFT-43 in BBSome-deficient mutants, indicating that they are mis-loaded onto IFT trains. This misloading allows them to bypass the ciliary gate. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) suggests the gate remains largely functional, supporting a potential two-step model of ciliary composition control: cargo selection/loading and ciliary gating. We propose that defects in cargo selection/loading (and potentially export) alter ciliary composition, allowing unintended protein entry.

title: Forced expression of UCP1 counteracts the compromised activity of NK cells in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) is a mitochondrial inner membrane protein that mediates non-shivering thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue. Natural killer cells are key effectors of antitumor immunity but are impaired in the tumor microenvironment. Here we show that UCP1 is downregulated in tumor-infiltrating NK cells (TINKs) from colorectal cancer patients and tumor-bearing mice and correlates with impaired effector function. Natural killer cell-specific UCP1 ablation accelerates tumor growth and reduces tumor infiltration. Transforming growth factor β1 and hypoxia repress UCP1 transcription through C/EBPβ downregulation. UCP1 deficiency increases CD36/FABP4-mediated fatty acid uptake and alters mitochondrial respiration, accompanied by mitochondrial damage, mitochondrial DNA release, NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Enforced UCP1 expression prevents tumor microenvironment-induced pyroptosis and maintains antitumor activity in murine models and patient-derived organoids. Genetically modified expression of UCP1 in NK cells is a potential therapy for patients with tumors.

title: Sexually dimorphic transdifferentiation of endothelial cells in atherosclerosis
abstract: Sex differences in atherosclerosis are clinically recognized, but the contribution of endothelial cell (EC) states and fates to these differences remain incompletely understood. Here, we used EC lineage tracing in male and female Apoe −/− /Cdh5-CreER T2 /Rosa26-mTmG mice fed a high-fat diet and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of plaque-bearing aortae. We identified nine sex-biased EC subpopulations, including capillary, lymphatic, Sox17 + , Myh11 + , Mki67 + , and Ly6a + ECs enriched in females and Col8a1 + and Fmo2 + ECs enriched in males. GeneTrajectory analysis and lineage tracing indicated that approximately one quarter of GFP⁺ EC-lineage cells transit into adipocyte-like, SMC-like, or fibroblast-like states. EC-to-SMC-like transitions were more prominent in females, whereas EC-to-adipocyte-like transitions were more prominent in males. Regulatory network analysis using pySCENIC implicated Klf2 and Creb5 in EC fate decisions. These findings reveal sex-specific EC-lineage trajectories associated with distinct plaque phenotypes and nominate candidates for sex-informed therapeutic investigation.

title: Quantitative imaging supports that endoskeletal mineralization in sharks is an adaptive trait
abstract: Modern sharks ( Selachimorpha ) exhibit a broad suite of adaptations that enable them to inhabit diverse marine environments. Notably, their cartilaginous endoskeleton displays varying degrees of mineralization, potentially reflecting adaptations for buoyancy, locomotion, and feeding. Here, quantitative computed tomography was applied to assess endoskeletal mineralization in representatives from all nine orders of sharks spanning 26 out of 35 families. Our findings reveal that skeletal mineralization is highly variable between species and is more closely associated with ecological factors such as depth distribution, than with phylogenetic relationship. We find that deeper-dwelling species generally exhibit lower degrees of mineralization, suggesting adaptations for buoyancy regulation and energy conservation. Our study provides insight into the variation of skeletal mineralization in the ecology and evolution of sharks.

title: Directed differentiation with mechanical simulation enhances alveolar-like features in human pluripotent stem cell-derived lung epithelium
abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived lung models remain limited by inefficient progenitor specification and incomplete alveolar maturation. Here, we present a robust and scalable differentiation strategy that reproducibly generates high-purity ( > 85%) fetal lung progenitors without cell sorting. These cells form distal bud tip organoids that recapitulate human fetal late tip and late stalk epithelial populations with multilineage potential. We show that direct co-culture with human lung fibroblasts, combined with Notch inhibition, promotes efficient differentiation toward fetal AT1- and AT2-like epithelial states, supported by transcriptional, protein, and ultrastructural analyses. Importantly, paracrine signaling alone is insufficient, highlighting a requirement for direct epithelial–mesenchymal interaction. We further integrated a microfluidic air-liquid interface culture system incorporating cyclic stretch. Under these conditions, we observed activation of mechanotransduction-associated and developmental signaling programs together with structural and transcriptional changes consistent with more mature alveolar-like epithelial states. This platform establishes a physiologically relevant model for human alveologenesis and provides a foundation for disease modeling and regenerative applications.

title: Targeting central thalamus with transcranial ultrasound reduces arousal in healthy volunteers
abstract: Using low-intensity focused transcranial ultrasound stimulation, we test the causal roles of the central thalamus in arousal and the pulvinar in visuospatial attention in the healthy human brain. In a within-subjects, counterbalanced design, 27 healthy volunteers (two females) complete a vigilance task (Psychomotor Vigilance Task) and a visuospatial attention task (Egly-Driver Task) before and after sham, central thalamic, and pulvinar sonication. Targeting the central thalamus slows responses and increases lapses in attention during the vigilance task, indicating reduced arousal. Pulvinar sonication reduces (and slows) responses to visual stimuli presented contralaterally, suggesting a disruption of contralateral visuospatial attention. These results provide causal evidence linking the pulvinar to visuospatial attention and the central thalamus to arousal in the healthy human brain and demonstrate that ultrasound can elicit distinct behavioral changes in healthy volunteers when delivered to close but functionally distinct thalamic regions, underscoring its potential as a tool for noninvasive brain mapping.

title: Whole brain modeling reveals subtype specific regulation for adolescent major depressive disorder
abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder exhibits substantial intrinsic subtype heterogeneity, necessitating the development of subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Using the Boston Adolescent Neuroimaging of Depression and Anxiety dataset, we identified two subtypes with distinct clinical features. For each subtype, we constructed a whole-brain model and performed virtual stimulation to assess regulatory effects at global (whole-brain) and regional (classical depression-related targets) levels. Here we show that the two subtypes require different but stable stimulation modalities, excitatory or inhibitory, to normalize brain activity. Optimal stimulation intensities for restoring static and dynamic features vary across targets and subtypes, whereas the stimulation modality remains consistent within each subtype. Notably, localized stimulation of subtype-specific targets within classical depression-related regions produces more effective and stable outcomes than whole-brain stimulation. These findings provide a computational framework for identifying subtype-specific regulatory strategies in adolescent major depressive disorder, bridging whole-brain modeling with potential clinical translation.

title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
abstract: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Results show that CMT Vglut2 neuron activity revealed a reduction during the loss of consciousness and a subsequent elevation upon recovery of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Chemogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 neurons delays induction and hastened recovery from sevoflurane anesthesia. Moreover, during sustained sevoflurane anesthesia at steady state, optogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 neurons facilitates cortical activation and behavioral recovery. During burst suppression under sevoflurane, this stimulation elicits cortical arousal and declines the burst-suppression ratio. Conversely, inhibiting CMT Vglut2 neurons via chemogenetic or optogenetic methods produces greater sensitivity to sevoflurane anesthesia and deepens cortical suppression, respectively. Monosynaptic connections from CMT Vglut2 neurons to red nucleus glutamatergic neurons (RN Vglut2 neurons) are identified using combined retrograde and anterograde tracing. During sevoflurane anesthesia, optogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 -RN terminals triggers cortical activation. Overall, these findings identify the CMT Vglut2 -RN pathway as a neural circuit regulating cortical activation and behavioral arousal under various stages of sevoflurane-induced anesthesia.

title: Efficient structural information integration into protein language models with implicit mixture-of-experts ProBEiT
abstract: Protein language models can now predict function and mutational effects directly from sequence, yet only a few incorporate function-deciding structural information with minimal additional effort. We introduce ProBEiT, a multimodal architecture that jointly encodes amino-acid sequences and discrete, tokenized structures via a parameter-efficient implicit mixture-of-experts scheme with deterministic routing. Trained on 1.7 million AlphaFoldDB proteins, the 400 million-parameter model surpasses larger baselines across six tasks of fitness prediction and functional annotation, demonstrating enhanced understanding of sequence-structure-function relationships. Unlike existing billion-scale models, ProBEiT attains strong accuracy early in continual training period, reducing computational cost. In an experimental thermostability engineering task on glycerol-3-phosphate oxidase, it correctly identifies optimized variants with positive epistatic effects. These results show that tightly coupling structural context with sequence modeling in a modality-specialized framework enables efficient, high-performance protein engineering.

title: Hierarchical distortions in structure-function coupling linked to multiscale neurobiological characteristics in autism
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is associated with widespread alterations in brain connectivity, but how structural and functional networks are jointly reorganized remains unclear. Here, we show that autism is associated with altered structure-function coupling, particularly in the hierarchical organization of sensory and association systems. Using brain imaging data from 91 individuals with autism and 67 typically developing controls, we model functional connectivity from structural networks using Riemannian optimization and examine communication across multiple steps. In the resulting simulated networks, hierarchical organization is comparable between groups at lower communication steps but becomes less differentiated in autism as communication extends across multiple steps. These alterations are associated with excitation/inhibition alterations, neurotransmitter distributions, gene expression, and multisensory processing. We also identify atypical connectivity involving the thalamus and putamen. Importantly, greater hierarchical distortion predicts more severe autistic symptoms, linking macroscale network organization with neurobiology and behavior. These findings highlight hierarchical structure-function coupling as a potential framework for understanding biological and behavioral characteristics in autism.

title: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting species B adenoviruses largely mimics the DSG2 receptor engagement mechanism
abstract: Species B human adenoviruses (B-HAdVs), including HAdV7, HAdV3, and the re-emerging HAdV55, cause severe respiratory disease and engage desmoglein-2 (DSG2) through their fiber knob. Here, we report the identification and structural characterization of two monoclonal antibodies, 5C5 and 6G7, raised against the HAdV7 fiber knob. Both antibodies neutralize HAdV7 and display cross-reactivity toward other B-HAdVs, with nanomolar affinities. Notably, 5C5 recognizes HAdV3 despite limited sequence conservation and exhibits greater neutralization potency than 6G7. Cryo-electron microscopy structures at 1.8 Å and 2.0 Å resolution for 6G7 and 5C5 respectively, reveal distinct binding modes: 6G7 engages the trimeric fiber knob at a 3:3 antibody: knob ratio, whereas 5C5 binds the apex at a 1:3 ratio. The 5C5 epitope overlaps with key DSG2-interacting residues, including a conserved pocket among B-HAdVs, providing a structural basis for its enhanced neutralization through receptor-binding blockade. These findings establish the fiber knob apex as a vulnerable site for antibody-mediated neutralization and identify 5C5 as a candidate targeting pathogenic species B adenoviruses.

title: Crocin alleviates renal fibrosis through inhibiting mitochondrial dysfunction via regulating HOXD8/PGC‑1α pathways
abstract: Crocin, a key bioactive compound derived from saffron ( Crocus sativus L .), a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible herb, exhibits renoprotective effects against fibrosis, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that homeobox D8 (HOXD8) and PGC1-α are downregulated, while reactive oxygen species levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and fibrosis are increased in kidney fibrosis models. HOXD8 overexpression increases PGC1-α expression, reduces reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial function, and suppresses profibrotic genes. Crocin upregulates HOXD8 and mitigates mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis. Mechanistically, HOXD8 binds the PGC1-α promoter and enhances its transcription. DNMT1-mediated promoter hypermethylation drives HOXD8 downregulation, and crocin reduces DNMT1 enrichment and activity at this promoter. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay support a potential interaction between crocin and HOXD8, and crocin reduces HOXD8 ubiquitination. These findings suggest that crocin upregulates HOXD8 by inhibiting both its promoter hypermethylation and protein ubiquitination, thereby ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

title: SUMOylation and ubiquitination of Viperin dynamically regulate the type I interferon-mediated antiviral response
abstract: Viperin is a broad-spectrum antiviral protein induced by interferon. Viperin in epithelial cells is regulated and degraded by E3 ubiquitin ligase UBE4A. Here, we observed that UBE4A expression was deficient in immune cells such as splenocytes and macrophages, and elucidated how the protein stability and antiviral activity of Viperin are regulated under the condition of UBE4A deficiency. Specifically, PJA2 mediates K48-linked polyubiquitination of Viperin at K358, leading to proteasomal degradation and enhanced viral susceptibility. Upon viral infection, host upregulation of RANBP2 enhances Viperin SUMO3-ylation, which competitively inhibits ubiquitination, thereby stabilizing Viperin and suppressing viral replication. However, prolonged infection recruits SENP1, causing deSUMOylation that promotes Viperin degradation and facilitates immune evasion. Viperin SUMOylation is modulated by small-molecule inhibitors such as Momordin-Ic and SENP1-IN-1. This study reveals a synergistic antiviral mechanism mediated by Viperin ubiquitination and SUMOylation, and further deepen the understanding of the protein homeostasis of Viperin and its role in the antiviral immune response.

title: Albendazole induces ferroptosis through the USP7-GPX4 axis in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
abstract: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) is an aggressive hematological malignancy that still requires the development of novel therapeutic strategies. Here, leveraging a drug-repurposing strategy, we performed a high-throughput screen of 3008 U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drugs and identified albendazole (ABZ), a benzimidazole anthelmintic, as a potent agent against B-ALL across multiple preclinical models. Mechanistically, ABZ directly binds ubiquitin-specific protease 7 (USP7) and triggers its autophagy-dependent destabilization, subsequently promoting the ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thereby inducing ferroptosis in B-ALL. Our study revealed that USP7 directly interacts with and stabilizes GPX4 by removing K48-linked ubiquitin chains, and both proteins are markedly upregulated in B-ALL patients, correlating with poor survival. Collectively, we identify a previously unrecognized USP7-GPX4 axis that governs ferroptosis and show that ABZ, as a novel ferroptosis inducer, triggers ferroptosis by targeting this axis, supporting clinical repurposing of albendazole or therapeutic targeting of USP7-GPX4 to improve B-ALL outcomes.

title: Lactate drives the emergence of tumor cells with centrosome amplification through CP110 lactylation
abstract: Centrosome amplification (CA) is a critical driver of tumor heterogeneity and subsequent cancer progression and metastasis. However, the cellular origin of CA has not been fully elucidated, specifically whether CA arises from progenitor cells with pre-existing centrosome abnormalities or develops de novo in initially normal tumor cells. In this study, we demonstrate that lactate, a metabolic feature commonly enriched in tumor tissues, induces the transformation of cells with two centrosomes into cells with CA, thereby providing an explanation for the widespread presence of CA in tumors. Mechanistically, through systematic screening of centrosomal proteins, we identified CP110 and its key lactylation site at lysine 690 (K690), as critical drivers of CA in tumor cells. Furthermore, CP110-K690 lactylation promotes genomic instability, accelerates cellular proliferation, and enhances metastatic potential by driving CA, collectively facilitating malignant progression. Importantly, inhibition of CP110-K690 lactylation effectively disrupts this pro-tumorigenic signaling axis. Collectively, these findings identify CP110-K690 lactylation as an upstream molecular mechanism underlying the pervasive occurrence of CA across diverse tumor types and its role in promoting aggressive tumor behavior.

title: eDNA and microscopy reveal traits underlying long-term zooplankton community change
abstract: Zooplankton form a vital link between phytoplankton and higher trophic levels, including commercially exploited fish, making recent declines in copepods and increases in meroplankton a major concern. To investigate underlying mechanisms, we compared weekly, high-resolution net (microscope analysis: 35 years) and surface water (eDNA: 11 years) from Station L4 in the Western English Channel. The two methods showed strong agreement for holoplanktonic crustaceans and gelatinous predators, but weaker correspondence for meroplankton. The far greater taxonomic insight from meroplankton groups provided by eDNA revealed a shift towards higher relative sequence abundance of soft sediment (mainly sublittoral) fauna, rather than from rocky nearshore. Trait-based analysis showed long-term increases were mainly fine filter feeders, including many meroplankton larvae. This suggests that changes in water column processes, linked to declining nutrient supply and a shift towards smaller phytoplankton, were contributing to broader changes in the pelagic food web and benthic-pelagic coupling.

title: AI-assisted image-based screening identifies TFEB agonists that restore adipose angiogenesis and reduce adipose fibrosis
abstract: Adipose tissue expansion in obesity frequently outpaces vascularization, triggering hypoxia, fibrosis, and metabolic dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms coordinating adaptive angiogenesis during this expansion remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that myeloid deletion of Transcription Factor EB ( Tfeb ) in high-fat diet-fed mice exacerbates epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) dysfunction, manifesting as profound hypoxia, fibrosis, and systemic insulin resistance. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal a novel TFEB-VEGFA axis: TFEB directly activates Vegfa transcription in macrophages, and its absence impairs angiogenic compensation under hypoxic stress. To translate these findings, we established an AI-driven, high-content screening platform to quantify TFEB nuclear translocation. We identified and validated Tetrandrine and Pacritinib as potent TFEB agonists. Notably, Tetrandrine acts via an mTOR-independent mechanism. Pharmacological activation of TFEB with these compounds restored adipose angiogenesis, resolved fibrosis, and improved insulin sensitivity in obese mice. These findings establish macrophage TFEB as a critical regulator of healthy adipose remodeling and validate the TFEB-VEGFA axis as a therapeutic target for metabolic diseases.

title: White matter fiber bundles enable robust conduction and time-critical signaling despite axon caliber variation
abstract: Axon caliber determines signal conduction velocity and varies within and across the bundles that form the brain’s wiring. Our knowledge of this organization derives largely from 2D histology, assuming cylindrical axons whose calibers are described by their radius. However, recent 3D histology reveals substantial along-axon variability in radius, calling into question 2D-derived insights into axon radius and conduction velocity. We show in 450,000 3D axon reconstructions from male rats that—despite this individual variation—axon bundles possess stable radius distributions at the ensemble level. These distributions are faithfully captured by 2D cross-sections and yield robust conduction velocity predictions, as along-axon variability has only a modest effect. Conduction in large axons is particularly stable, supporting time-critical signaling. With 2D sampling validated, we leverage 46 million human corpus callosum axons from 2D histology to determine sample size requirements across neuroscience applications. Our findings show how axonal organization gives rise to stable ensemble statistics and conduction, explaining and reinforcing decades of 2D histology-based research.

title: Genetic interaction between Adgrg6 and Sox9 reveals a feedforward mechanism for postnatal spinal stability
abstract: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most common pediatric spinal disorder and is best understood as a complex polygenic condition. Genome-wide association studies have identified AIS risk loci, including regions near ADGRG6 and SOX9 , yet the mechanisms underlying its heritability remain poorly defined. Here we use spatial transcriptomics to characterize gene expression in the spine of a conditional Adgrg6 mutant mouse model, revealing reduced expression of Sox9 and several extracellular matrix genes in the intervertebral disc. We demonstrate a strong genetic interaction between conditional loss of Adgrg6 and a hypomorphic Sox9 allele that increases the penetrance and severity of scoliosis. We further show that SOX9 occupies open chromatin within the Adgrg6 locus in SOX9+ cells isolated from the mouse disc tissue, consistent with direct transcriptional regulation, and provide evidence for SOX9-dependent and SOX9-independent regulation across a variety of spinal tissues. Together, these findings support a self-reinforcing feedforward circuit in which Adgrg6 and Sox9 are co-regulated to maintain extracellular matrix gene expression in the annulus fibrosus and paraspinal tissues. These results provide mechanistic insight into genes implicated by AIS-associated loci and establish combined Adgrg6–Sox9 insufficiency in mice as a tractable model of polygenic scoliosis susceptibility.

title: Automated and noninvasive in vivo mapping of brain functions in the human cortex
abstract: Mapping forms the basis for understanding the functional organization of the brain and for developing targeted interventions in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive tool that allows causal mapping of cortical functions involved in motor control, speech, and connectivity. Since manual mapping procedures limit standardization, we present an automated cortical mapping method that integrates electronically controlled multi-locus TMS with a Bayesian optimization algorithm for identifying stimulation targets efficiently and objectively through a closed-loop framework. We localized individual motor representation area peaks with high accuracy (average 2.4 mm and 5° deviation from the optimum) in only approximately 4 minutes. This represents a substantial advancement over current mapping approaches, providing the means to greatly accelerate and standardize both research and clinical protocols while maintaining high reliability. We anticipate that our approach can further extend to map other cortical functions that cannot be easily analyzed online by a human operator.

title: Exceptional preservation in cherts reveals complex cuticular architecture in one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoans
abstract: Ecdysozoans, animals characterized by a periodically moulted cuticle, became major components of Cambrian marine ecosystems, yet the structural organization of their earliest non-mineralized cuticles remains poorly documented. Here we report Spinosoma reticulatus gen. et sp. nov., a millimeter-scale ecdysozoan from Fortunian cherts on two paleogeographic blocks: the Liuchapo Formation, South China, and the Yurtus Formation, Tarim Block, dating to ca. 538 Ma. This occurrence represents one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoan body-fossil records and may predate the classic Kuanchuanpu scalidophoran assemblages. The material preserves a terminal mouth with large circumoral spines and abundant cuticular fragments. Its cuticle comprises a fibrous mesh, short upright plate-like structures, and hollow ridged spines. Morphological and Raman data support an ecdysozoan affinity, whereas scalidophoran placement remains tentative. Spinosoma reveals a previously undocumented cuticular architecture, suggesting that early ecdysozoan ecological breadth and integument diversity are underestimated in the earliest phase of the Cambrian Explosion.

title: A NEST-based framework unlocks massively parallel simulation of networks of multi-compartment neurons with customizable subcellular dynamics
abstract: While subcellular mechanisms in the dendrites of neurons govern the implementation of learning and memory in the brain, large-scale network simulations featuring such processes remain challenging to achieve. This can be attributed to a lack of appropriate software tools, as neuroscientific simulators focus on the one hand on highly detailed models, and on the other hand on massive networks featuring point neurons. Here, we fill this gap by implementing a framework for the massively parallel simulation of simplified dendrite models with customizable subcellular dynamics. We leverage the NEural Simulation Tool (NEST), the neuroscientific reference with respect to efficient massively parallel simulations of point-neuron networks. By co-opting the model description language NESTML, we generate C++ code implementing user-configurable subcellular dynamics. We show that the generated models run efficiently, leading to scalable NEST network simulations. To showcase relevant functionalities, we provide a proof-of-concept demonstration that a key sensory computation – the association of top-down context arriving at distal dendrites in layer 1 and feedforward sensory input arriving perisomatically – can be achieved in a single-shot fashion through apical calcium dynamics. Our work thus unlocks the study of how dendritic processes shape network function and learning at scale.

title: SQSTM1/p62-LC3A–mediated autophagic clearance of stress granules prevents apoptosis under hyperosmotic stress
abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are transient, membraneless assemblies that form in response to cellular stress and typically disassemble when stress resolves. Their persistence has been linked to neurodegenerative disease. Here we show that LC3A has a selective role in the autophagic clearance of SGs formed during hyperosmotic stress. LC3A, but not LC3B or LC3C, associates with SGs, and depletion of LC3A impairs their removal. LC3A also promotes clearance of pathogenic inclusions containing TDP-43 or poly(GR) dipeptides from C9orf72 expansions. Proteomic analysis reveals enrichment of the autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 in SGs, supporting its role in SG degradation. SGs are also enriched in mitochondrial and apoptosis-related proteins, consistent with an anti-apoptotic function potentially linked to mitochondrial proximity. However, prolonged stress activates CASP3 and promotes apoptosis, which is exacerbated by defective SG clearance. These findings highlight the critical role of the SQSTM1–LC3A axis in SG turnover and cell survival under chronic stress.

title: Mercury contamination impairs the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis of a neotropical caiman
abstract: The capacity to regulate corticosterone release following a stressful event is an essential component of the physiological flexibility required to maintain homeostasis and ensure adaptive responses to environmental change. We show that wild smooth-fronted caimans with elevated blood mercury (Hg) concentrations exhibited reduced peak corticosterone levels during standardized stress tests, indicating a dampened maximal stress response. Hg blood concentrations were negatively correlated with corticosterone responsiveness, suggesting impairment of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis function. These results demonstrate that environmental Hg contamination is associated with reduced stress responsiveness and physiological flexibility, which likely limits the ability of Hg-contaminated individuals to cope with novel environmental stressors. We found that a methylmercury-sensitive cysteine in the glucocorticoid receptor is highly conserved across vertebrates, suggesting a shared molecular mechanism for mercury effects on glucocorticoid signaling. Given the widespread Hg pollution in tropical ecosystems, these findings emphasize the role of Hg as an endocrine-disrupting chemical in crocodylians.

title: PDE10A identified by cross-hemisphere visual cortex proteomics restores adult ocular dominance plasticity involving cAMP/CREB signaling
abstract: Ocular dominance plasticity (ODP) is robust during the critical period but is restricted in adulthood. The molecular programs that distinguish this permissive state and whether they can be pharmacologically engaged in adulthood remain unclear. Here, using quantitative proteomics of the left and right visual cortices from monocularly deprived (MD) juvenile mice, we identify phosphodiesterase 10 A (PDE10A) and the cAMP signaling pathway as molecular signatures of juvenile ODP. Juvenile MD is associated with reduced PDE10A and increased phosphorylated CREB (pCREB) in the visual cortex contralateral to the deprived eye, whereas adult mice show no comparable response. In adult mice, systemic administration of the selective PDE10A inhibitor TAK-063 during MD reinstates an experience-dependent ocular dominance shift and reduces visual acuity in the deprived eye. This is accompanied by increased cortical cAMP and pPKA, an inverted-U pCREB response peaking at 0.3 mg/kg, and upregulation of plasticity-related synaptic proteins. TAK-063 does not alter basal visual function, retinal electrophysiology, or locomotor behavior in non-deprived adults, excluding nonspecific sensory/motor confounds. These findings identify PDE10A as a candidate molecular regulator of visual cortical plasticity and support its pharmacological inhibition as a strategy to facilitate experience-dependent plasticity in the adult visual cortex.

title: CRISPR knockout screen identifies MYD88/IRAK4 signaling as a mediator of deoxynivalenol-induced oxidative damage
abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a prevalent mycotoxin that poses serious risks to food and feed safety, particularly affecting pigs. However, the primary host factors mediating DON cytotoxicity remain poorly understood. Here, we perform a genome-wide CRISPR knockout (KO) screen in porcine intestinal epithelial IPI-2I cells and identify MYD88 and IRAK4 as the top-ranked genes conferring resilience to DON-induced cell death. DON treatment activates the MYD88/IRAK4/NF-κB signaling axis, leading to pronounced upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNFα. Concomitantly, DON suppresses the expression of multiple antioxidant genes (e.g., GPX4, SOD1, NQO1, GCLC) and promotes accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidized protein. Genetic KO of MYD88 or IRAK4 markedly reduces IL-1β expression, partially restores antioxidant protein levels, attenuates ROS and oxidized protein accumulation, and significantly improves cell viability upon DON exposure. Our findings establish the MYD88/IRAK4 signaling cascade as a critical driver of DON-triggered inflammatory and oxidative damage, revealing potential therapeutic targets for mitigating mycotoxin toxicity in livestock.

title: Circuit plasticity coordinates action selection and temporal compression during operant conditioning in Aplysia
abstract: A central challenge in neuroscience is to explain how reinforcement jointly shapes action selection and the temporal structure of action execution to optimize behavioral efficiency. Using an ex vivo operant conditioning paradigm in the Aplysia feeding circuit, we found that reinforcement biases selection toward ingestive motor programs and shortens their duration by advancing the transition from protraction to retraction phases of the feeding movements. Temporal compression reflected coordinated plasticity of phase-switch elements. Operant conditioning reduced the intrinsic electrical excitability of neuron B52 and thereby weakened B52-mediated inhibition of the retraction-initiating interneuron B64, while also lowering the threshold for triggering the B64 plateau potential. Phase-restricted co-manipulation of B52 and B64 activity reproduced protraction shortening. These results provide a circuit-level framework for how reinforcement coordinates motor-pattern selection with temporal structure within identified circuitry, a form of circuit plasticity that may contribute to the efficiency of action execution.

title: TOC159 receptors use a galactolipid-specific bipartite signal for chloroplast targeting in Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Chloroplast biogenesis and function depend on the recognition and import of nucleus-encoded preproteins by the translocon at the outer envelope membrane of chloroplasts (TOC), yet the mechanism by which TOC159 receptors, key components of the TOC complex, are targeted and inserted remains only partially understood. Here we show the C-terminus of TOC159 from Arabidopsis thaliana contains a highly conserved bipartite chloroplast targeting signal, composed of a canonical β-signal and “reverse transit peptide-like” extension that shares canonical chloroplast transit peptide characteristics in reverse orientation. Using chloroplast targeting assays in planta and peptide-lipid interaction assays in vitro, we demonstrate that the β-signal is required for targeting, whereas the reverse transit peptide-like extension is not required, but contributes significantly to targeting fidelity through interactions with galactolipids enriched in plastid membranes. These findings support an evolutionary adaptation in TOC159 targeting, combining β-signal-driven insertion with galactolipid-specific recognition that couples TOC159 targeting to TOC complex assembly and provides a mechanism for organelle discrimination in plant cells.

title: M6A demethylation of IRF9 by ALKBH5 promotes intervertebral disc degeneration via nucleus pulposus cell necroptosis
abstract: The intervertebral disc endures many stresses, and death of its nucleus pulposus cells drives disc degeneration. Here we show that a form of programmed cell death called necroptosis increases in degenerated nucleus pulposus cells after stimulation by tumour necrosis factor alpha. The enzyme AlkB homolog 5 removes a chemical mark called N6-methyladenosine from the messenger RNA of interferon regulatory factor 9, stabilising the messenger RNA and raising the level of this protein. Interferon regulatory factor 9 then directly activates the promoters of receptor-interacting protein kinase 1, receptor-interacting protein kinase 3, and mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein, increasing their expression. Silencing AlkB homolog 5 or interferon regulatory factor 9 reduces necroptosis and slows disc degeneration in animals. These findings indicate that N6-methyladenosine-mediated necroptosis is important in disc degeneration, and targeting this pathway may offer a therapeutic option.

title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation promotes arthritis resolution by modulating joint cell phenotype involving E-series resolvins
abstract: The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. Non-classical monocytes and VCAM-1 + synovial fibroblasts were lower at peak arthritis while pro-resolution MerTK + CD206 + macrophages were increased at resolution onset. Lipid mediator profiling of arthritic paws identified a distinct repertoire of molecules in ω3-fed mice, with elevated EPA-derived resolvin E2 (RvE2) and RvE4, compared with increased TXB 2 and PGF 2α with a normal diet. Pharmacological treatment of mice with RvE2 and RvE4 concomitant with arthritis induction, attenuated arthritis and increased MerTK + CD206 + macrophages in arthritic joints. Synovial explant treatment revealed reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and enzyme release including IL-6, CCL2 and MMP-9. In arthritic patient blood, RvE2 and RvE4 (100 nM) lowered monocyte ICAM-1 expression. Collectively, these data identify cellular and molecular determinants of an ω3 diet in pre-clinical and human settings, highlighting therapeutic potential.

title: Myristic acid promotes in vitro maturation and developmental competence of porcine oocytes
abstract: The present study examined how antral follicle size influences oocyte meiotic maturation and developmental competence from a metabolic perspective and explored strategies to improve the meiotic maturation and quality of oocytes derived from small antral follicles. Untargeted metabolomics revealed dynamic metabolic changes during porcine antral follicle development, with increased fatty acid synthesis and enhanced activities of related enzymes in oocytes from larger follicles. In vitro, myristic acid (MA) improved meiotic maturation (polar body extrusion, spindle morphology, chromosome dynamics) and survival of oocytes from small follicles by reducing Annexin V expression and ROS levels. MA also enhanced their developmental competence after parthenogenetic activation. Molecular and cytochemical analyses showed that MA altered the transcriptional profile, increased lipid storage, and boosted mitochondrial number and function. Finally, MA upregulated SIRT1, activated PPARα, and increased CPT2 expression, suggesting a potential mechanism underlying its effects on these oocytes.

title: Structure-function tethering of human locus coeruleus connectivity reveals a noradrenergic cortical hierarchy
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is the primary source of cerebral norepinephrine and plays a broad role in cognition. Here, we show the macroscale organization of human LC connectivity using 7 T diffusion and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Structural and functional connectivity exhibit a dominant rostral-caudal gradient, with structure-function tethering lowest in the intermediate LC and increasing toward its rostral and caudal portions. In the neocortex, this pattern is expressed as steeply increasing tethering from the central sulcus toward anterior and posterior regions. Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas tracing further reveals preferential LC projections to somatomotor cortex. The cortical expression of LC structure-function tethering exhibits a network-level hierarchy and aligns with a behavioral axis. Additionally, this cortical expression shows significant spatial covariance with norepinephrine transporter concentration, fiber length, and gray matter volume. Together, these findings provide MRI-based evidence for a hierarchical macroscale organization of human LC connectivity linking structural and functional architecture to cortical and behavioral variation.

title: OVOL1/2 regulate trophectoderm differentiation during the morula-to-blastocyst transition
abstract: The blastocyst formation rate of human embryos cultured in vitro for assisted reproduction is approximately 50%, with most embryos arresting at the cleavage stage; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of biopsied blastomeres from morphologically high-quality 8-cell embryos and tracked the developmental progression of the remaining embryos to the blastocyst stage. Embryos that failed to form blastocysts exhibited impaired zygotic genome activation (ZGA). We identified OVOL1/2 as critical ZGA genes that were markedly underactivated in these embryos. Functional analyses in both mouse and human embryos demonstrate that depletion of OVOL1/2 disrupts trophectoderm differentiation via ARPC1B-dependent mechanisms, thereby impairing the morula-to-blastocyst transition. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insights into preimplantation embryonic development and reveal potential causes of blastocyst formation failure.

title: Metabolic sensor Gpr35 links dietary lipids to itch mediating neural circuits
abstract: Impact of nutrition on systemic health is well-recognized but the specific sensors that couple western dietary lipid metabolites into the pathological triggers of chronic itch and inflammation remain elusive. Here, we identify a metabolic- to-sensory axis in which 9-keto-12,13-epoxy octadecenoic acid (EKODE), an endogenous dietary linoleic acid derivative acts as a potent ligand for the G protein-coupled receptor 35 ( Gpr35 ) to drive chronic itch, inflammation, and heat hypersensitivity. We demonstrate that Gpr35 is selectively expresses in a distinct population of sensory neurons and genetic ablation of Gpr35 in sensory neurons attenuates EKODE and psoriasis-associated itch and inflammation. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of Gpr35 significantly attenuates itch in mouse models of psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. We show that Gpr35 signaling engages the itch-specific brain natriuretic peptide, defining a labeled-line pathway that is functionally distinct from classical nociceptive circuits. Collectively, our findings establish Gpr35 as a critical neuro-metabolic sensor in healthy and disease conditions.

title: Aberrant RNA sensing and host-specific immunopathology in highly pathogenic influenza infections
abstract: Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage.
