However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. We also discuss perspectives on influenza viral polymerase compatibility with host factors and species-specific RNA-sensing mechanisms as critical determinants of the pathological outcome during highly pathogenic influenza infections.

title: Towards a sequential microbiome therapy for HPV-associated cervicovaginal dysbiosis
abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are the principal cause of cervical cancer, and are increasingly associated with ecological instability of the cervicovaginal microbiome. Multiomics studies indicate that hrHPV persistence is linked to reduced Lactobacillus dominance, increased anaerobic taxa, and metabolic alterations that may compromise epithelial integrity and antiviral immunity. In this Perspective article, we introduce a sequential microbiome therapy (SMT) framework designed to restore cervicovaginal ecological balance and support viral clearance. SMT is a two-phase, strain-resolved strategy. The first phase targets dysbiotic communities using antimicrobials, biofilm-disrupting or microbiota-modulating approaches to create a window for ecological reset. The second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species selected for their acidification capacity, competitive fitness, and ability to stabilize the mucosal environment. We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. The platform’s utility is exemplified through various use cases, including antimicrobial resistance tracking, biomarker prediction, microbiome classification, and functional annotation of key microbes. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

title: BdCDPK5 is an essential regulator of Babesia divergens intraerythrocytic progression
abstract: Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) are central regulators of developmental transitions in apicomplexan parasites, yet their roles in tick-borne pathogen Babesia remain largely uncharacterized. Using Babesia divergens , a zoonotic parasite of growing medical and veterinary concern, we identify BdCDPK5 as an essential enzyme controlling intraerythrocytic parasite replication. Through comprehensive transcriptional profiling of the bdcdpk repertoire across synchronized blood-stages, combined with an animal-free Ixodes ricinus membrane feeding infection model, we show that bdcdpk5 is dominantly expressed during vector tissue colonization and significantly upregulated upon erythrocyte invasion. Genetic disruption of BdCDPK5 caused long-term growth arrest and pronounced morphological defects, whereas its ectopic expression promoted parasite replication. Localization analyses further revealed BdCDPK5 to be diffusely distributed throughout the parasite cytoplasm and associated with vesicle-like structures within infected erythrocytes. Together, these findings establish BdCDPK5 as a molecular determinant of B. divergens intraerythrocytic infection and highlight it as a promising target for selective therapeutic intervention.

title: Evolutionary genomics of ancient and endangered Achnatherum breviaristatum on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
abstract: Climate change and human activities threaten biodiversity on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), renowned for its endemic species. We examined genomic diversity and evolution of Achnatherum breviaristatum , an endangered grass species endemic to the QTP. A. breviaristatum diverged from its sister lineage ~15 million years ago, and contrasts with two widespread and ecologically dominant monotypic genera within the same lineage— Neotrinia splendens and Psammochloa villosa —which thrive in arid northwestern China. Using newly generated chromosome-level genome assemblies and population resequencing data for A. breviaristatum and N. splendens , together with publicly available genomic data for P. villosa , we reveal that A. breviaristatum exhibits lower genetic diversity and heterozygosity based on resequencing reads mapped to the respective reference genomes. All species experienced parallel demographic declines since the Quaternary glaciation, with reductions during the Pleistocene. The endangered status of A. breviaristatum likely results from weaker clonal reproduction relative to its relatives, combined with Pleistocene vegetation shifts and anthropogenic activities. A reduced genetic load in A. breviaristatum may mitigate the effects of its low genetic diversity and contribute to its persistence. This study highlights interactions among climatic shifts, reproductive strategy, and human impact in shaping endemic species’ fates, providing genetic insights for conservation in vulnerable ecosystems.

title: Developmental restriction of the jaw skeletal muscle cardiogenic potential
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of mortality worldwide and heart failure remains an end-stage disease with no other treatment than transplantation. A promising field to tackle heart failure is cardiomyocyte implantation. Whereas cardiomyocyte generation from pluripotent cells has shown promising results, direct derivation of cardiomyocytes from somatic stem cells is still challenging. Skeletal muscle progenitors have been extensively studied as a source of cardiac cells, due to their cellular and functional similarities. During development, the right ventricular myocardium and jaw skeletal muscles derive from a common pool of myogenic mesodermal progenitors. Previous studies have reported the derivation of cardiomyocyte-like cells specifically from adult mouse jaw muscle stem cell populations, but not from other skeletal muscles, suggesting that developmental origin endows cardiogenic potential. Here we evaluated the cardiogenic potential of satellite cells and mesenchymal progenitor cells from the masticatory muscle by reproducing, optimizing and diversifying previously described protocols. We consistently found that stem cells from masticatory muscles are unable to differentiate into cardiac cells under any tested cardiogenic environment. Furthermore, pharmacological erasing of repressive epigenetic marks did not activate cardiogenic potential, suggesting that barriers restraining lineage plasticity are profound and unlikely to be reversed by simple exposure to cardiogenic environments.

title: Cleavage of xanthone and flavone C–glycosidic bonds by the enzyme complex LaGME from gut Lachnospiraceae
abstract: Aglycones, the bioactive metabolites of C– glycosides, can be obtained through the deglycosylation of naturally abundant C– glycosides. However, C– glycosides are more resistant to enzymatic and chemical degradation. Gut microbiota and its enzymes are known to cleave the C–C glycosidic bond, but only a limited number of active strains and functional enzymes have been identified. Here we show that a new C– deglycosylation gene cluster encoding the g lycoside- m etabolizing e nzyme from La chnospiraceae (LaGME), an enzyme complex consisting of a C – g lycoside o xidoreductase (LaCGO1) and a C – g lycoside e limination enzyme complex (LaCGE), was discovered using the DUF6379 domain-containing protein as a probe. LaGME demonstrates significant activities toward xanthone-type and flavone-type C– glycosides. After investigation into heterologous expression, structural determination and catalytic mechanism, a LaGME-mediated one-pot cascade enzymatic reaction system was developed for green production of aglycones. This research provides an approach to uncover C– glycoside-metabolizing enzymes in nature, as well as a preliminary basis for the sustainable production of value-added bioactive aglycones from glycosides.

title: Analysis of 515 human proteomes defines plasma extracellular vesicle core composition, corona and coisolated networks
abstract: Plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, yet their proteomic profiling remains confounded by massive co-isolation. Here, we resolve this heterogeneity through a meta-analysis of 515 human plasma EV proteomes. We demonstrate that the reproducible core proteome is overwhelmingly governed by predictable, surface-charge-driven mass-action that dynamically mirrors synthetic nanoparticle corona formation. By quantitatively decomposing the core isolate against pan-synthetic coronas and agonist-induced platelet EVs, we trace the core isolate to three main mechanistic origins: an electrostatic plasma corona, ex vivo platelet vesiculation and biological macromolecular co-isolates. Crucially, the residual vesicular cargo strongly correlates with thrombin-induced platelet degranulation, indicating that phlebotomy-induced trauma contribute to the bulk signal. We provide a modular atlas that mathematically distinguishes biophysical coronas from these cellular co-isolates, establishing a new framework for interpreting biological origin in plasma EV proteomics.

title: Tamoxifen targets Wisp2 to impair subcutaneous adipocyte progenitor self-renewal and adipogenic differentiation
abstract: Breast cancer endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, systemically disrupts estrogen receptor signaling and increases type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk in women. Hyperplastic adipose tissue expansion, especially in subcutaneous depots, facilitates nutrient storage and attenuates inflammation during a chronic positive energy balance and is impaired in the absence of estrogen. Adipocyte progenitors are renewed through Wnt signaling pathway activation, however the the mechanisms that explain the depletion of these cells during endocrine therapy are not defined. Here we show the direct impact of tamoxifen on proliferation, renewal, and differentiation in subcutaneous adipose stromal cells from humans and adult mice. In obesity, the Wnt1 inducible signaling pathway protein 2 (Wisp2) was lost in adipocyte progenitors following endocrine therapy. Wisp2 gain and loss of function studies defined the link between estrogen signaling and adipocyte progenitor maintenance. We found that tamoxifen treatment disrupts the protection of adipocyte progenitors by estrogen, mediated through suppression of Wisp2. These studies reveal effects of tamoxifen therapy that precede and could influence T2D development in breast cancer survivors.

title: Assessing whole-cortex excitability from electromagnetic brain signals
abstract: Cortical excitability is a core feature of brain function shaped by microcircuitry, large-scale networks, and neurochemistry. In humans, it can be inferred from indirect electrophysiological measures, yet it remains unclear whether these capture a single construct or multiple processes. We systematically compared established excitability metrics using whole-head magneto-encephalography (MEG) recorded at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation in a large sample of healthy adults. These measures included stimulus-driven synchronization, spectral power, aperiodic (1/f) activity, signal complexity, long-range temporal correlations, and phase–gamma synchronization. Hierarchical clustering identified six distinct excitability dimensions with limited redundancy, indicating that cortical excitability is inherently multidimensional. Aperiodic and alpha-band measures were strongly coupled and most spatially aligned with stimulus responses, while temporal, complexity, and synchronization metrics were largely independent. Regional differences were most pronounced in integrative and internally oriented areas. Each dimension also related differently to cortical morphology and neurotransmitter receptor density, highlighting diverse neurobiological substrates and supporting multimodal approaches to studying excitability.

title: Single-cell atlas reveals NLRP2 associated mitochondrial dysfunction in estrogen induced Macrobrachium nipponense sex reversal
abstract: Sex reversal is used in aquaculture breeding, but its cellular basis in crustaceans remains unclear. Here we combine estrogen induced feminization, single-cell RNA sequencing, histology and RNA interference to study gonadal development in the oriental river prawn ( Macrobrachium nipponense ). Feeding post-larval males with 17β-estradiol produced neo-females with ovary like gonads. Single-cell profiling of testes, ovaries and neo-female gonads resolved major oogenic and spermatogenic cell types and showed that neo-female gonads were enriched in early germ cells, whereas mature oocytes and spermatozoa were depleted. Cell type matched analyses identified oxidative phosphorylation as a consistently altered pathway. The gene MnNLRP2 showed primary spermatocyte specific and testis enriched expression. Knockdown of MnNLRP2 shifted sex ratios toward females in juveniles, altered sex hormone levels and caused spermatogenic arrest in adults. These results link MnNLRP2 to mitochondrial dysfunction during incomplete crustacean sex reversal.

title: Breaking new ground into RAD51 BRC repeats interplay in homologous recombination
abstract: Homologous recombination (HR) is a critical repair pathway involving numerous proteins that ensure error-free DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) repair. Dysfunction in HR components can compromise genome integrity. Despite advances, many aspects of HR remain poorly understood. Notably, even one of the earliest identified and most critical interactions, between RAD51 and BRCA2, remains incompletely characterized, mainly due to the lack of structural data. This study presents a comprehensive biophysical analysis of the RAD51–BRC repeats interaction, integrating computational and experimental approaches. Starting with assessing the correlation between the binding affinities of individual BRC repeats and their impact on RAD51 disassembly, our investigation extends to larger BRCA2 truncations, offering unprecedented insights into the molecular determinants of RAD51 recognition. As mutations in the BRC repeats impair RAD51 recruitment and are associated with cancer, these results provide a valuable framework for interpreting pathogenic variants and guiding precision medicine therapies.

title: Ultra large docking reveals novel chemotypes and a distinct binding mode for Porcupine inhibition
abstract: Wnt signaling is essential for embryonic development and adult tissue homeostasis, and its dysregulation contributes to cancer and other human diseases. Porcupine (PORCN), a membrane-bound O-acyltransferase (MBOAT) required for Wnt palmitoylation and secretion, has emerged as an important therapeutic target. Despite promising preclinical results, PORCN inhibitors have shown limited clinical activity to date, motivating the search for new chemotypes and binding modes. Here, we docked a library of 1.3 billion molecules against PORCN and identified 16 novel compounds that inhibit Wnt signaling. These hits are structurally distinct from known PORCN inhibitors, and structure-based optimization of one series yielded sub-micromolar leads. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that the lead inhibitor binds PORCN in an unreported mode within the palmitoleoyl-CoA chamber, positioned closer to the cytosol than existing inhibitors. Together, our findings expand the chemical and structural space available for targeting PORCN and provide new starting points for development of Wnt signaling antagonists.

title: Kidney-derived mitochondrial extracellular vesicles trigger acute lung injury in sepsis via mtDNA-cGAS-STING in pulmonary endothelium
abstract: Sepsis often leads to multiple organ failure, but how injury in one organ propagates to another remains poorly understood. Here we show that the injured kidney releases mitochondria-rich extracellular vesicles (mitoEVs) into the circulation, which travel to the lung and trigger acute lung injury. In septic mice and cultured renal tubular epithelial cells, sepsis promotes the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles by upregulating sorting nexin 9. Blocking this process in kidney tubules reduces the release of mitoEVs and protects against lung injury. Once taken up by lung endothelial cells, the mitochondrial DNA carried by these vesicles activates an innate immune pathway involving cGAS and STING, with ZBP1 serving as a potential cooperative partner for this activation. This leads to endothelial barrier disruption, immune cell recruitment, and respiratory failure. In patients with sepsis, higher levels of circulating mitoEVs associate with lung injury and death. These findings identify a kidney-to-lung signaling axis that may be targeted therapeutically.

title: Genome-wide analyses reveal recent diversification and hidden diversity in Amazonian howler monkeys, including two new species
abstract: Complex ecological and evolutionary patterns shaped the rich biodiversity of the Neotropics. Understanding how diversity emerges and is maintained is key to anticipating potential biotic responses to current anthropogenic changes. Howler monkeys ( Alouatta ) are one of the most successful radiations inhabiting this region. However, 11 of the 16 taxa currently recognised are classified as threatened by the IUCN Red List, and the genus faces increasing threats from deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and hunting. Here, we present a genomic-wide analysis covering 11 of the 13 recognised Alouatta species. Our results indicate that most of this genus’ diversity in Amazonia originated in the last million years, driven by major biogeographic and ecological factors, such as geographical barriers (e.g., Amazonian rivers, and the Andes), as well as by ecological gradients, including savanna-forest mosaics and ecotonal zones. Historical biogeographic reconstructions support a trans-Andean origin for Alouatta . Based on integrative taxonomy, including genomic and morphological evidence from numerous specimens, we formally identify groups and provide descriptions for two new species. Our findings underscore the power of genome-wide data to uncover hidden diversity and to inform conservation strategies, particularly in rapidly transforming tropical ecosystems where undescribed species may already be at risk.

title: A mMono-Bac1.0 system for recombinant adeno-associated virus vectors with higher flexibility, throughput and yield
abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) holds immense promise for therapeutic applications, but high production costs limit its widespread clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for manufacturing breakthroughs. Here, we establish a modular Mono-Bac system with the p24 -NanoLuciferase (Nluc) reporter Bacmid for rAAV production, named mMono-Bac1.0, enhancing manufacturing flexibility, throughput and yield simultaneously. The system introduces two key technology to the pFD/Cap-(ITR-GOI)-Rep transfer vector-based Mono-Bac framework. First, a modular pGB-AAV Donor construction strategy enables one-step all-in-one AAV transfer vector assembly and effortless switching of capsids or GOIs, thus facilitating high-throughput combinatorial production. Second, an engineered p24 -Nluc Bacmid enables rapid (<5 min) quantification of infectious recombinant baculovirus (rBV) titers and real-time monitoring of Nluc activity in culture supernatants to determine the optimal harvest point (log RLU ~ 6.5), thereby maximizing rAAV yield. This system has the potential to advance baculovirus expression vector (BEV)-based rAAV manufacturing into a data-driven era, supporting efficient industrial-scale production.

title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
abstract: Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. Phylogenetic reconstructions reveal early aureochrome diversification in the stramenopile lineage, originating in a heterotrophic ancestor before photosynthesis was acquired. This challenges the assumption that aureochromes are restricted to phototrophs, suggesting an ancestral role in spectral light signaling. We find that, despite changes in light quality and photoperiod by latitude, diatom aureochrome domain architecture remains conserved. This implies adaptation through regulatory tuning, such as altered expression dynamics or post-translational control. Our results emphasise the importance of spectral-light sensing in polar oceans and link the widespread dominance of aureochromes to their ancient origin and conservation.

title: Chronic exercise induces a pathway-dependent electrophysiological signature in the mouse hippocampus
abstract: Chronic physical exercise enhances hippocampal function, yet its impact on network activity remains poorly defined. We explored whether treadmill running leaves durable imprints detectable through electrophysiological techniques and spatial transcriptomics. Field potentials (FPs) were recorded in anesthetized male C57BL/6 J mice after a chronic exercise protocol. Using machine learning to analyze FP generators, we were able to reliably classify animals into their correct group by Lateral Perforant Path (LPP) activity alone. Classification rested on a multifeatured signature rather than any single feature. Schaffer Collateral and Lacunosum-Moleculare generators showed changes that did not achieve statistical significance. Exploratory spatial transcriptomics identified a coordinated enrichment of calcium signaling and long-term potentiation programs in the dentate gyrus. These findings demonstrate that exercise-induced plasticity is not a global shift but a localized remodeling of specific synaptic inputs, with changes detectable at both circuit and molecular levels. These durable, pathway-specific imprints persist in the absence of active task engagement, suggesting a reorganization of the brain’s memory circuitry.

title: Specification of bone marrow sinusoids requires TIE2-mediated positive feedback involving COUP-TFII and VEGFR3
abstract: The bone marrow (BM) vascular network drives bone development and hematopoiesis, but the mechanisms governing its specialized sinusoidal architecture remain poorly characterized. Here, we show that the angiopoietin receptor TIE2 is highly expressed by BM sinusoidal endothelial cells (BM-SECs). Its endothelial deletion triggers sinusoidal capillarization, characterized by reduced vessel diameter and aberrant mural cell coverage. Mechanistically, TIE2 insufficiency downregulates VEGFR3 in BM-SECs within 48 h of induced endothelial Tek deletion, while leaving hepatic sinusoidal VEGFR3 unaffected. RNA-sequencing reveals that TIE2 insufficiency suppresses sinusoidal development pathways while upregulating arterial and angiogenic genes. We validate this phenotype using inducible Tek deletion mainly in VEGFR3 + SECs and in Angpt1 -insufficient mice. Furthermore, endothelial deletion of the transcription factor COUP-TFII ( Nr2f2 ) recapitulates these defects, reducing both BM sinusoidal TIE2 and VEGFR3 expression. Finally, induced endothelial deletion of Flt4 produces a similar phenotype. Together, our findings imply that ANGPT1/TIE2 and COUP-TFII form a reciprocal regulatory loop essential for BM sinusoidal specification by sustaining VEGFR3 expression.

title: Developmental and genetic modulation of evidence integration dynamics in zebrafish sensorimotor decision-making
abstract: Animals integrate information over time and maintain persistent internal representations of cues to guide decision-making. How the underlying behavioral algorithms of individual animals depend on factors such as experience, developmental stage, or genotype remains poorly understood. Drift-diffusion models provide a powerful theoretical framework to describe and predict performance metrics across a wide range of species. The stochastic nature of these models and the typically limited throughput of most experimental designs challenge the automatic inference of latent variables. Here, we combine high-throughput behavioral assays in larval zebrafish with drift-diffusion modeling, revealing that larvae progressively develop more persistent, self-reinforcing integration dynamics during early development. This effect is reduced in fish carrying mutations in genes linked to human epilepsy and schizophrenia. Our results show that behavior-based drift-diffusion modeling can offer a scalable, automated approach to generate experimentally testable hypotheses about the algorithmic implementation of sensorimotor integration in health and disease.

title: Cortex-wide neuronal dynamics underpin quasi-periodic patterns in resting-state fMRI
abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) captures whole-brain activity fluctuations non-invasively in humans and animals. Beyond task/stimuli-locked responses, fMRI measures large-scale patterned activity during rest. Among these, quasi-periodic patterns (QPPs) represent recurring waves of activity that unfold over seconds and exhibit consistent spatiotemporal characteristics. Notably, certain fMRI-QPPs are well-preserved across species and altered in various neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases. Yet, our collective understanding of their neural underpinnings is limited given the indirect nature of the blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) fMRI signal. Simultaneous measures of local field potentials have provided some affirmation that fMRI-QPPs have neural origins, but these point-measurements are limited to a handful of sites. Here, we use a unique multimodal implementation of simultaneous wide-field calcium (WF-Ca 2+ ) imaging and fMRI to investigate the neural origins of fMRI-based QPPs. We uncover a robust time-locked correlation between QPPs detected by cortex-wide fluorescent WF-Ca 2+ imaging of neural activity and QPPs of BOLD-fMRI. These data validate the hypothesis that BOLD-fMRI QPPs derive from preceding slow waves of neural activity with regional and temporal precision.

title: Epigenetic regulation of cancer drivers and EMT revealed by genome-wide methylome profiling in NSCLC
abstract: Carcinogenesis is driven by dynamic and heterogeneous epigenomic alterations promoting tumour evolution and affecting therapeutic resistance. We performed genome-wide DNA methylation sequencing (RRBS) on 260 lung methylomes from 130 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. Here we show that gene-body hypomethylation involved lung cancer drivers, while promoter hypomethylation targeted miRNA genes linked to EGFR signalling, EMT, and PD-L1 regulation. Upstream transcription factor analysis also implicated epigenetic control of EMT, EGFR and immune pathways, through SNAIL, SLUG, SMAD3 and BRD4 . Promoter hypermethylation represented multi-gene epi-oncodriver mechanism associated with GPCRs. Subtype-specific patterns were additionally observed: adenocarcinoma showed alterations in neurotransmitter signalling, whereas squamous cell carcinoma embraced canonical oncogenic pathways. We provide a genome-wide methylome analysis in NSCLC, revealing epigenetic alterations that may contribute to tumour progression and therapeutic resistance linked to EGFR , EMT and immunological responses. These findings highlight the translational potential of epigenetic profiling to inform clinical strategies in NSCLC.

title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
abstract: Sea stars achieve strong yet reversible underwater adhesion using a duo-gland system in their tube feet. While adhesive sea star footprint proteins (Sfps) are well characterized in Asterias rubens , comparable molecular data for other asteroids are limited. Here, we generated a high-quality de novo genome assembly of the starlet cushion star, Asterina gibbosa , enabling full-length gene identification of Sfps. Proteomics of deposited footprint material identified 34 candidates; in situ hybridization localized 10 to the tube foot adhesive epidermis. Nine (designated Agib-Sfps) were homologous to known A. rubens Sfps, and one encoded a trypsin-like proteinase. Anti-peptide antibodies revealed distinct footprint labeling patterns for Agib-Sfp7 and Agib-Sfp8, although mostly associated to the thin layer in contact with the substrate. Comparative analyses indicate a conserved core adhesive toolkit and domain repertoire between species, alongside species-specific reshuffling of domains across Sfps. These results refine the molecular model of asteroid adhesion and provide targets for sequence recombinant production toward seawater-compatible biomimetic adhesives.

title: Disruption of arn lipid A aminoarabinosylation confers AmpCmediated cephalosporin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in chronic cystic fibrosis infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa is shaped by pathogen-specific adaptation, yet the mechanisms driving cephalosporin resistance in epidemic clinical lineages remain incompletely defined. Here, we used in vitro experimental evolution to generate ceftazidime-resistant P. aeruginosa LESB58 strains, revealing loss-of-function mutations in the arnBCADTEF-ugd operon, encoding the L-Ara4N lipid A modification system (aminoarabinosylation). Loss of the arn operon in LESB58 conferred high-level resistance to ceftazidime, cefepime, and ceftolozane. Transcriptome sequencing and an ampC -promoter reporter fusion demonstrated strong upregulation of ampC , encoding a β-lactamase, following ceftazidime treatment in the arn deletion strain. Deletion of ampC in the arn mutant restored cephalosporin susceptibility to wild-type levels, confirming AmpC as the primary resistance mechanism. This arn -linked resistance was also observed in LESB65 but absent in laboratory strains PAO1 and PA14. These findings identify a connection between lipid A modification loss and AmpC-driven cephalosporin resistance in clinically relevant P. aeruginosa lineages.

title: COX2 contributes to the spatial reorganization of B7H4+ and CD44v6+ niches promoting therapy resistance in ER- breast cancer
abstract: Estrogen receptor-negative (ER-) breast tumors are aggressive subtypes with limited therapeutic options. Cyclooxygenase-2 promotes chronic inflammation, immune suppression, and therapeutic resistance. Whether COX2 signaling organizes tumor microenvironments across oxygen gradients remains unclear. Restricted Exchange Environment Chambers (REECs) were used to explore the COX2 impact on spatial tumor architecture across oxygen gradients. Baseline COX2+, B7H4+, and CD44v6+ cells exhibited distinct distributions, with CD44v6 predominance. Inflammatory stimulation increased and spatially reorganized COX2+, B7H4+, and COX2+CD44v6+ populations. While COX2+ cells occupied oxygenated-to-intermediate zones, B7H4+ populations were enriched in intermediate-to-hypoxic regions, and CD44v6 remained broadly distributed. Diclofenac disrupted this organization and reduced clustering of COX2+, B7H4+, and COX2+CD44v6+ phenotypes. Poor-outcome patients showed high COX2 at the tumor-stroma interface as well as altered COX2+, B7H4+, and CD44v6+ clustering phenotypes. These findings identify COX2-dependent microenvironments as clinically relevant features of therapeutic resistance. Diclofenac preferentially depleted hypoxic compartments preserved following cisplatin treatment alone, supporting the targeting of spatially organized inflammatory niches to improve therapeutic response.

title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
abstract: Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when making mate-choice decisions under uncertainty, yet how such advice is integrated into decision-making remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) computational model best fit the behavioral data, indicating that social influence arises from reciprocal interaction rather than one-way transmission. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more strongly influenced decision-making. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that task-level INS robustly forecasted overall advice influence. Together, these findings demonstrate that friend advice influence emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice influence mate-choice decision.

title: Analysis of structural modifications and metagenomic sequencing during the ensiling of Caragana korshinskii provides insights into how extrusion pretreatment promotes lignocellulose degradation
abstract: In this study, to address the problems of poor silage fermentation quality and difficulty degrading lignocellulose interfering with resource utilization of Caragana korshinskii biomass, the effects of extrusion pretreatment (temperature 140°C and screw speed of 400 rpm) on its ensiling process were investigated. Results showed that pretreatment significantly improved silage quality, with lactic acid and water-soluble carbohydrate content increasing significantly ( P < 0.05), neutral detergent fiber content decreasing significantly ( P < 0.05), and hemicellulose degradation rate increasing by 31.64 ± 1.20% compared with the normal silage group. Microstructure analysis showed that pretreatment destroyed the dense biomass structure, increased specific surface area and porosityenhanced hydrophilicity, and reduced crystallinity, thus promoting the degradation of hemicellulose and cellulose. Metagenomic analysis further showed that extrusion pretreatment remodeled the microbial community structure, increasing the proportion of lactic acid bacteria such as Weissella and Companilactobacillus , and significantly increased the abundance of genes encoding debranching enzymes (CE3 and CE12) involved in hemicellulose degradation as well as main chain hydrolases (GH43 and GH8) ( P < 0.05). This study provides insights into the mechanisms by which extrusion pretreatment improves Caragana korshinskii silage in terms of physical and chemical structure and microbial functions, and this in turn may provide a technical and theoretical basis for understanding how efficient ensiling can be achieved more broadly in high-lignocellulosic feedstocks.

title: Widening the BRCAness therapeutic window for its synthetic lethality effects with PARP inhibitors
abstract: This review examines the expanding role of PARP inhibitors in cancer therapy, moving beyond the traditional model of single-strand break repair inhibition and BRCA-dependent synthetic lethality. We highlight emerging evidence that PARP inhibitors induce cytotoxicity through replication-associated DNA damage, including defects in Okazaki fragment maturation and replication gap accumulation. By integrating recent mechanistic insights with findings from CRISPR-based screens, we outline how disruptions in DNA replication and repair pathways define a broader BRCAness phenotype. We further emphasize the clinical implications of these discoveries, including novel combination strategies that extend the therapeutic applicability of PARP inhibitors beyond prevailing treatment regimens.

title: iTBS and cTBS to an individualized dlPFC target produce differential working memory improvement and session-dependent putamen deactivation
abstract: We evaluated the effects of individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) theta-burst stimulation (TBS) on working memory performance and task-related BOLD activity in 115 healthy adults (iTBS: n = 63; cTBS: n = 52). Stimulation was delivered to an individually-localized left dlPFC target identified using task-based fMRI, with each TBS visit consisting of five 600-pulse trains delivered as either the intermittent (iTBS) or continuous (cTBS) protocol. Participants completed the Sternberg Working Memory paradigm at baseline and approximately 24 hours after each visit. Groups were well-matched at baseline on all behavioral and neural measures. iTBS produced a significant improvement in working memory accuracy across sessions while cTBS did not, with a significant Group × Session interaction confirming differential trajectories. Both groups showed reaction time speedup across sessions, consistent with a shared practice effect. Despite these behavioral differences, BOLD activity at the dlPFC stimulation site showed no significant effects of Group, Session, or their interaction. Whole-brain analyses revealed significant session-dependent attenuation of bilateral putamen deactivation during the retention interval in both stimulation groups, with greater putamen deactivation at baseline correlating negatively with working memory accuracy. These results demonstrate that individualized task-based fMRI targeting can link TBS to circuit-level behavioral change, and that downstream subcortical responses may be more sensitive indices of TBS effects than activation at the stimulation site. The absence of a sham condition limits causal inference; observed differences reflect stimulation pattern rather than absolute TBS effects.

title: Predicting discrete traits in evolving systems
abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. Predictions using discrete data are central to imputation, forecasting, and hypothesis testing in biology. How much accuracy and confidence they deliver together, and how this varies across scenarios and taxa, has not been quantified systematically. Here, using accuracy and log loss, we benchmark these models across scenarios varying in tree size, evolutionary rate, and trait coevolution. Against non-phylogenetic baselines, they increase accuracy by 23 percentage points and lower log loss by 92% on average; different Markov implementations perform similarly. Log loss rises as terminal branch lengths elongate, a direct consequence of the Markov process. Last, we provide a tutorial and empirical demonstration for the evolution of unexpected character states (outliers). Our study provides a framework for imputing missing data, reconstructing ancestral traits, and testing evolutionary hypotheses.

title: Genetic insights into foveal morphology and its associations with pigmentation and age-related macular degeneration
authors: On behalf of the UK Biobank Eye and Vision Consortium
abstract: The fovea is the small depression at the neurosensory retina that underlies high-resolution central vision. It is vulnerable to disease and disruption of its architecture can lead to visual disability. Foveal morphology varies substantially across individuals but the molecular causes and functional consequences of this variation remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyse six foveal morphological parameters derived from optical coherence tomography (OCT) images of 39,521 UK Biobank participants. We find marked variation in foveal morphology and identify significant associations with sex and genetic ancestry. Genome-wide association studies identify 162 lead loci across the six foveal morphological parameters, implicating genes involved in pigmentation (including TYR , TSPAN10 and GPR143 ) and developmental patterning (including FGFR2 , CYP26C1 and CYP1A1 ). Heritability estimates range from 29 to 43%. Foveal pit volume is associated with future risk of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) (hazard ratio 1.09, p = 0.026), a finding supported by Mendelian randomisation. Given the strong correlations among foveal traits, the specificify of this association to pit volume remains unclear. These results establish foveal morphology as a highly heritable trait that is biologically linked to AMD.

title: Genomic taxonomy reveals distinct evolutionary architectures within the Enterobacter cloacae complex
abstract: The Enterobacter cloacae complex is a major nosocomial pathogen group, yet its taxonomy remains poorly resolved below the species level, obscuring the evolutionary drivers of virulence and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show, by analyzing 254 clinical isolates from Taiwan alongside 6,493 public genomes, that a genome-resolved taxonomic framework corrects taxonomic assignments for 54.9% of public genomes, primarily by resolving Enterobacter hormaechei into its five subspecies. Subspecies-level resolution reveals two distinct evolutionary patterns. Virulence determinants and intrinsic resistance genes are strongly associated with subspecies identity and remain globally conserved, including near-universal carriage of the salmochelin locus in E. hormaechei subsp. steigerwaltii and strict linkage of chromosomal AmpC β-lactamases to specific species. By contrast, acquired carbapenemases show pronounced geographic variation independent of taxonomy. These findings demonstrate that subspecies represent the fundamental biological and epidemiological units within the Enterobacter cloacae complex and highlight the importance of subspecies-resolved genomics for diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and global surveillance.

title: Biofilm selection activates c-di-GMP synthesis by the bifunctional enzyme MbaA
abstract: Biofilms, in which microbes are encased within a self-produced matrix, represent the primary mode of microbial life. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing biofilm formation remains incomplete, limiting the development of targeted interventions against biofilm-associated infections. By selecting for Vibrio cholerae biofilms, we identified mutations in the polyamine-regulated, bifunctional enzyme MbaA that alter its enzymatic activity in metabolizing the conserved second messenger cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP). These mutations occur in both the c-di-GMP-producing GGDEF domain and the c-di-GMP-hydrolyzing EAL domain of MbaA. Mutagenesis and enzyme kinetic analyses revealed regulatory crosstalk between these domains, where mutations in either domain enhanced production of c-di-GMP by MbaA while concurrently reducing its hydrolytic activity. In the wild-type enzyme, c-di-GMP metabolism is post-translationally regulated by specific polyamines. Biofilm-selected mutations not only shift MbaA’s enzymatic activity but also disrupt this regulation, rendering the enzyme insensitive to external polyamine signaling. Our findings illustrate how evolutionary pressure can rewire existing enzymes, promoting a biofilm-associated lifestyle.

title: Early-life adversity induces social anxiety and cognitive deficits alongside neurobiological changes in rats
abstract: Mood disorders such as anxiety often originate early in life, yet rodent models of early-life adversity are typically assessed only in adulthood using a limited array of behavioral assays. Here we show how neonatal isolation affects social behavior, learning and memory, neuron structure, and blood metabolites in Long Evans rats ( Rattus norvegicus ). Juvenile isolated rats play less with unfamiliar peers but interact typically with cage mates, consistent with a social anxiety-like phenotype. As adults, isolated rats show reduced cooperation and increased aggression, whereas traditional anxiety tests do not reveal increased generalized anxiety. Females show pronounced cognitive and motivational deficits. Isolation is also associated with reduced dendritic spine density in the medial prefrontal cortex, sex-specific neuronal changes in the dorsolateral septum, and shifts in glucose and amino acid metabolism. Together, these findings reveal selective, sex-dependent consequences of early-life social deprivation across behavioral, neural, and metabolic domains.

title: Canonical correlation analysis identifies single nucleotide polymorphism combinations and gene expression associated with membranous nephropathy
abstract: In membranous nephropathy (MN), an autoimmune kidney condition, univariate genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified Human Leucocyte Antigen ( HLA ) and M-type phospholipase A2 receptor ( PLA2R1 ) genetic risk variants. Multivariate-single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) canonical correlation analysis (CCA) with transcriptomics analysis, can uncover additional insights within this context. We applied CCA to our National Unified Renal Translational Research Enterprise (NURTuRE)- chronic kidney disease (CKD) and Salford Kidney Study (SKS) European datasets, identifying 1095 HLA and 46 PLA2R1 SNPs showing significant MN correlation, and single-cell gene enrichment. Top SNP combinations showed greater significance in both MN by multivariate-SNP CCA, and MN and diabetic nephropathy (Type 1) by allele frequency analysis compared to healthy and non-MN groups. ATF6B , C2, CYP21A2 , and HLA-DRB1 colocalised with top HLA SNPs and showed significant differential expression in MN (published immune transcriptomics datasets). HLA-DQB1, HLA-DRB5 and RNF5 showed significant differential expression with lead SNP genotype status in MN and CKD. These previously unreported SNP and gene results are candidates for MN and potentially Type 1 diabetic nephropathy risk prediction.

title: Susceptibility of Achromobacter spp. to bacteriophages and phage/antibiotic combinations
abstract: Achromobacter infections pose significant challenges to people with Cystic Fibrosis (CF). It is a growing problem in people with CF because it is difficult to eliminate with antibiotics, leading to chronic lung infections that increasingly acquire antibiotic resistance. Here we identified a cadre of 26 bacteriophages that target clinical Achromobacter isolates. We tested these phages against a collection of 56 Achromobacter isolates and found that all were susceptible to multiple of these phages. We also evaluated whether we could restore the activity of certain antibiotics by using them as adjunctive therapy to phages in vitro. We found that when meropenem (a beta lactam antibiotic) was added to the phages, improved susceptibility (decreased MICs) was demonstrated in many isolates regardless of whether the Achromobacter was initially susceptible to meropenem. The data presented here suggests that combination therapy using meropenem with an active phage should be considered for treatment of Achromobacter infections regardless of pre-existing antibiotic susceptibility.

title: Melatonin regulates LIN-42/PERIOD through its receptor PCDR-1 to promote dark adaptation in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Organisms that live in lightless spatial niches (e.g., caves or soil) develop a daily clock using other senses, such as taste, smell, temperature, or mechanical senses. However, how these organisms, which experience only muted daily environmental cycles, use a circadian clock to adapt to darkness is worth exploring. In this study, we found that lin-42 /PERIOD was highly expressed in worms grown in darkness. lin-42 knockdown induced a phenotype of accelerated aging in worms under dark conditions. Melatonin inhibited the production of reactive oxygen species through its receptor, PCDR-1, thus maintaining lin-42 expression in darkness. Conversely, daylight inhibited lin-42 expression by ROS production due to suppression of melatonin synthesis. Moreover, we found that insufficient melatonin synthesis or lin-42 deficiency activated the transcription factor DAF-16/FOXO, which induced lipid accumulation in the worms. Our results suggest that the molecular network composed of melatonin and the LIN-42/PERIOD enables C. elegans to adapt to darkness.

title: Tracing the origin of non-brittle rachis TtBTR1 alleles in wheat
abstract: The evolution of non-brittle rachises, controlled by the TtBTR1 genes, was a key step during wheat domestication. Here, using k -mer-based approaches applied to a large diversity panel, we refine previous estimates of the geographical and temporal origins of the three known Ttbtr1 loss-of-function alleles and show that they emerged in distinct wild emmer subpopulations. For this, we generated a chromosome-scale dika wheat assembly carrying the recently discovered Ttbtr1-Ab allele. Our analyses reveal that the Ttbtr1-A alleles reside on an introgression from the southern judaicum wild emmer population into northern wild emmer wheat, providing an explanation for the long-standing debate about the Ttbtr1-A origin. We further demonstrate that the Ttbtr1-Aa and Ttbtr1-B alleles are already present in wild emmer wheat, with evidence indicating that they arose prior to the advent of agriculture. Together, these findings support a model in which key domestication genes in domesticated crops were selected and combined from standing genetic variation in wild relatives.

title: Directional blood flow within a shared capillary network links the nucleus of the solitary tract and area postrema in rats
abstract: Capillary networks are classically viewed as passive conduits that supply energy to active neural tissue. Whether microvascular organization can also contribute to functional communication between adjacent brain regions remains largely unexplored. The nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS) and area postrema (AP) form a brainstem complex that coordinates homeostatic regulation; however, the organization and functional significance of their shared microcirculation remain unknown. Previous anatomical studies identified direct capillary connections between the NTS and AP, demonstrating a continuous microvascular network between two anatomically distinct regions. Here, we used in vivo two-photon microscopy, combined with fluorescent vascular labeling and analysis of red blood cell dynamics, to investigate the blood flow within the shared NTS-AP microvasculature. Blood flow across these junctions is predominantly unidirectional, flowing from the NTS towards AP. Morphometric analyses reveal that AP capillaries are significantly larger than those in the NTS, providing a structural basis for this flow asymmetry. Despite these geometric differences, capillary flow velocities are preserved across regions, indicating active regulation of perfusion within the shared network. These findings reveal directional blood flow within a shared AP-NTS capillary network, identifying a potential vascular route by which diffusible signals generated in one region may preferentially reach the other.

title: Nutrient-dependent bet-hedging between reproduction and sporulation in Bacillus subtilis
abstract: To thrive in nature, bacteria must constantly balance growth with long-term survival in response to nutrient availability. Although sporulation in Bacillus subtilis is a classical survival strategy, how the sporulation program is regulated by nutrient conditions during exponential growth remains elusive. Here we show that the Spo0A-mediated sporulation program is strongly modulated during exponential phase across different carbon sources and is accompanied by pronounced population heterogeneity on poor carbons. We further identify the transition-state regulator AbrB as a key modulator that integrates growth and sporulation, promoting growth under favorable conditions while facilitating sporulation under poor nutrients. On good carbon sources, AbrB optimizes cellular resource allocation by directly suppressing the unnecessary expression of adaptive pathways. In contrast, on poor carbon sources, where the Spo0A-signaling pathway is strongly activated, AbrB promotes sporulation by repressing the expression of a plasmid-encoded Rap-family phosphatase gene, which otherwise interferes with the Spo0A signaling pathway. Together, these findings reveal a dual-control strategy that fine-tunes the trade-off between growth and survival and promotes bet-hedging under poor growth conditions, with important implications for both fundamental biology and synthetic biology.

title: Structural analysis of the specificity of three neutralising human monoclonal antibodies against poliovirus
abstract: Despite a global eradication programme, pathogenic polioviruses (PVs) still circulate, dictating a need for improved vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics. Understanding their antigenic properties has been based largely on studies in mice. Here we study three human monoclonal antibodies specific for the native conformation and either PV1, 2 or 3, determining high-resolution structures of complexes with virus-like particles. The anti-PV1 and anti-PV2 Fabs bind around the icosahedral 3-fold axes, whilst the anti-PV3 Fab binds the canyon. We reveal the basis of serotype specificity and discrimination between native and expanded antigenic states. The anti-PV3 antibody partly penetrates the canyon and makes numerous serotype specific interactions on the south canyon face, distinguishing it from a pan-serotype and pan-antigenic state PV antibody. These structures show that human antibodies often span more than one classical antigenic site and can bind deeper crevices than murine antibodies, expanding our understanding of the antigenic landscape of PV capsids and potentially informing the design of better reagents, antivirals and vaccines against PV.

title: FAK- and TGF-β1-dependent biomechanical alterations in microvascular endothelial cells exposed to fluid shear stress gradients
abstract: Endothelial cells (EC) form a dynamic monolayer barrier that regulates vascular permeability and is highly sensitive to mechanical cues, including shear stresses (SS) generated by blood flow. While spatial shear stress gradients (SSG) are linked to vascular pathologies such as atherosclerosis, their direct effects on cellular biomechanics across EC subtypes remain underexplored. Here, using an impinging flow device compatible with videomicroscopy, we demonstrate that exposure of two EC types to SSG causes an immediate and sustained two-fold decrease in migration speed, accompanied by enhanced coordination of collective motion and directional migration against the flow. Concurrently, EC traction and monolayer stresses increase acutely upon flow onset and continue to rise linearly over time. Mechanistically, FAK-mediated mechanotransduction governs flow-opposed migration, whereas the time-dependent increase in traction depends on TGF-β1 signaling and actomyosin contractility. Together, these findings identify SSG as key regulators of EC mechanics, collective dynamics, and signaling, with important implications for vascular disease diagnostics and therapeutics.

title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of quiescent epimastigotes as a resource for investigating Trypanosoma cruzi persistence
abstract: Chagas disease is caused by infection with the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi . Despite triggering a strong immune response, infections are typically life-long and can result in severe cardiac and/or digestive tract pathology. Current drugs have limited efficacy, and treatment failure is a common outcome. Eliminating a non-replicating T. cruzi sub-population that can persist after therapy has been a key challenge for the drug-development community. Here, we describe the transcriptome and proteome profiles of a low-proliferative sub-population of epimastigote forms of the parasite isolated from exponentially growing cultures on the basis of reduced turnover of transiently-induced red fluorescent protein. This partially quiescent sub-population was characterised by down-regulation of genes/proteins involved in translation, transcription, metabolism, mitochondrial function and DNA replication, and by up-regulation of proteins that promote exit from the cell cycle in other organisms. Differential expression was considerably more pronounced at a protein than an RNA level. These data provide a resource that can be exploited to dissect the mechanistic basis of quiescence, as a step towards refining the drug-development screening cascade.

title: Mathematical and experimental models of interactions among subclones and immunity in melanoma
abstract: Melanoma tumors often contain heterogeneous subclones, typically with proliferative or invasive phenotypes. These subclones interact with each other and the immune system to shape tumor progression. Understanding interactions between subclones and the tumor microenvironment is a fundamental challenge for melanoma treatment. To analyze such interactions, we developed dedicated in vivo melanoma mouse and mathematical models. In the experimental models, admixtures of proliferative and invasive subclones of varying proportions were implanted into immunocompromised and immunocompetent mice. Tumor growth and subclone composition were tracked over time. In parallel, we built a computational model to capture the system dynamics. By estimating parameter values of our mathematical model using experimental measurements, we found that, while the proliferative subclone outgrew the invasive subclone, T cell activities selected for the invasive subclone. Initial subclonal proportion in this dynamic system determines the overall tumor sensitivity to immune response. The key interactions identified in this study provide insights into how intratumor heterogeneity and immune pressure influence melanoma progression, suggesting strategies for optimizing individualized therapy.

title: CD30 ligand promotes skin wound healing through keratinocyte signaling and Vγ6+ γδ T-cell responses
A dichotomous family of Cache domain proteins evolved through c-type heme acquisition
abstract: Abstract PAS domains often bind cofactors, whereas related Cache domains are thought to function exclusively as ligand-binding modules. We identify and characterize a large family of Cache domains containing covalently bound c-type heme. Sequence, phylogenetic and structual analysis of the DUF3365/Tll0287 family reveals conservation of a canonical CXXCH heme-binding motif, establishing c-type heme binding as a defining feature of this family. Despite previous annotation as PAS-like, these proteins share a distinct heme-binding insertion into a pre-existing Cache scaffold, representing the first documented recruitment of an intact cofactor-binding motif into a bacterial sensor domain. Domain architecture further divides the family into two subclasses: one exhibiting fusions to signaling domains and another comprised of standalone proteins. Spectroscopic analyses indicate that a representative signaling protein acts as a nitric oxide sensor, whereas a stand-alone representative exhibits redox-related properties and weak nitric oxide binding. These findings expand the functional repertoire of Cache domains and reveal a mechanism for the evolution of bacterial sensory systems.

title: Dynamic climate and ecological expansion drive body morphology evolution in fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods
abstract: Cephalopods originated in the Cambrian approximately 500 million years ago, evolving from externally shelled ancestors to forms with diverse morphologies. Despite their morphological diversity, the macroevolutionary patterns and drivers of their diversification remain incompletely understood. Here, we construct a time-calibrated phylogenetic framework for fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods and quantify evolutionary rates and morphological disparity over ~490 million years. We identify five peaks in morphological diversification, indicating rapid evolutionary phases during historical periods. Morphological disparity exhibits a time-lagged response to evolutionary rate shifts. Sea surface temperature and ecological factors are macroevolutionary drivers shaping evolutionary rates and morphological disparity. Major environmental perturbations, including the end–Permian and end–Triassic mass extinctions and Early Triassic and Toarcian hyperthermal events, are associated with reduced evolutionary rates, whereas post–Cretaceous conditions correspond to elevated rates driven by ecological release and adaptive radiation. Our results show that cephalopod morphological evolution is governed by coupled environmental and ecological processes that structure evolutionary dynamics over deep time.

title: Glutathione S transferase assembled gold silver nanoclusters activate cGAS STING immunity in breast cancer
abstract: Breast cancer often returns or spreads after treatment, and therapies that can destroy tumors while also engaging the immune system are urgently needed. However, it remains difficult to design safe nanomaterials that both heat tumors under light and turn dying cancer cells into signals that support long-lasting antitumor immunity. Here we show that glutathione S-transferase guided self-assembly produces ultrasmall glutathione-stabilized gold-silver nanoclusters for laser-assisted breast cancer treatment. Under near-infrared light, these nanoclusters efficiently generate heat and oxidative stress, killing breast cancer cells and releasing immune-stimulating signals. The treatment activates the cGAS-STING immune signaling pathway, promotes dendritic cell maturation, increases tumor-killing T cell infiltration, and strengthens memory T cell responses. In mouse models of primary and metastatic breast cancer, the nanoclusters preferentially accumulate in tumors and suppress tumor growth, metastasis, and relapse with limited signs of toxicity. This protein-guided nanocluster strategy provides a potential route for combining localized light-based treatment with systemic antitumor immunity and may support the future development of safer and more durable cancer nanomedicines.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
abstract: Introgression is increasingly documented, yet its detection remains challenging because patterns used to infer gene flow may reflect multiple processes, including the persistence of ancestral polymorphism under balancing selection. Domestic species, like goats, and their wild relatives provide informative models for testing the biological feasibility and genomic consequences of interspecific gene flow. We analyze whole-genome sequences from 164 individuals of the genus Capra , including 36 newly generated, to investigate hybridization and signatures of introgression within the genus. Genomic analyses confirm a goat–ibex hybrid and identify two backcross offspring, providing evidence of male F1 fertility. Further analyses involving domestic goats ( Capra hircus ), their ancestor the bezoar ( C. aegagrus ), and three ibex species ( C. ibex , C. pyrenaica , and C. sibirica ) revealed patterns consistent with both pre- and post-domestication introgression. We identify 8 candidate regions with shared haplotypes consistent with ancient introgression predating domestication and enriched for genes involved in olfaction and immunity. However, some regions show signatures compatible with balancing selection. Overall, our results show that hybridization between domestic and wild Capra is biologically possible, that most shared haplotypes likely predate domestication, and highlight the importance of distinguishing introgression from balancing selection when interpreting shared genomic variation across species.
